articleTitle: Counter-TEMPEST: Information Spoofing based on the EM-leakage Signature of TMDS System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper proposes a new approach to counter the TEMPEST attack, which is one of the information theft methods using leakage electromagnetic waves. As various signal processing techniques and new algorithms have made existing response systems no longer effective, this paper imitates the leaked signal itself through the generation rules of the representative video signal protocol, TMDS, and simple source modeling. Based on this, this paper hypothesize a scenario for what kind of signal the TEMPEST attacker would collect if our leaked signal were radiated. The main scenario is to deceive the TEMPEST assailant by including intentionally wrong or strange information in our imitated leaked signal, which is called "Spoofing" as a strategy term. To experimentally validate such an approach, a TEMPEST system is constructed, and the results of the experiment are discussed briefly.

articleTitle: TEMPEST Demo for Increasing Awareness
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: TEMPEST is a special topic within the electromagnetic environmental effects domain and refers to spying on information systems through leaking electromagnetic fields. The major difference with electromagnetic interference is that for TEMPEST we are also interested in the information contained in the leaked electromagnet fields. Modern and low-cost software defined radios and huge amount of processing power is readily available, and this has been used to develop a TEMPEST demonstrator. The development and use of such a SDR-based TEMPEST demonstrator for HDMI and DVI-D has been described in this paper.

articleTitle: Influence of Return Current Cable Arrangement on Ringing Damped Oscillations in Contact Discharge Calibration Waveform from ESD Generator
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: We measure contact discharge current waveforms from an ESD generator with a test voltage of 4 kV in different arrangements of a 2 m long return current cable in order to clarify the effect of ringing damped oscillations that appear in the contact discharge calibration waveforms. The spectral features of ringing are investigated based on the spectral characteristics of composite waveforms of the measured contact discharge waveform combined with the ideal contact discharge current waveform without ringing (IEC specified waveform) given in IEC 61000-4-2, in view of the measured input impedances of one-ended grounding cable. The result shows that the ringing damped oscillations of contact discharge waveforms cause the spectra from 20 MHz to 200 MHz, but the spectra in the frequency range from 40 MHz to 200 MHz differ greatly depending on the measurement environment and cable arrangements, which hardly affect the spectra from 20 MHz to 40 MHz and over 200 MHz. The frequencies of the multiple peaks and dips alternately appearing in the spectra from 40 MHz to 200 MHz roughly correspond to the resonance frequencies of the measured cable input impedances. This concludes that the ringing damped oscillations should mainly come from the distributed resonances of the return current cable.

articleTitle: Characteristics of 3D Printed SIW Filter Incorporated with Artificial Dielectric Material
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Filter is an essential component in wireless communication systems. As continuous development of these systems, there is a growing need for compact and lightweight components. The use of substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) structure can assist to reduce losses at high frequencies while also minimizing the component size. Furthermore, the use of artificial dielectric material (ADM) structures can also reduce the size of radio frequency (RF) component without compromising its performance. However, combination of these structures can make the fabrication process more complex and significantly increase the weight of filter. Therefore, a 3D printing technology is utilized to manufacture SIW filter with ADM incorporation. After the manufacturing and conductive paint coating processes, a prototype of 3D printed polylactid acid (PLA) based SIW filter incorporated with ADM structure is experimentally characterized, in which it operates at multiple frequency bands with the center frequencies of 2.71 GHz, 3.835 GHz, and 5.14 GHz, and the bandwidth responses of 135 MHz, 315 MHz, and 900 MHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Variability of Conducted Emissions of EV Chargers due to Mutual Effects on a DC Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: DC grids are becoming a popular choice to cope with highly dynamic and distorting loads, such as electric vehicle chargers that feature significant conducted emissions in the supraharmonic range, on/off load profiles and large power levels (especially for fast charging mode, enabled by connection to a DC grid). One major factor affecting the reliable assessment of emissions in the supraharmonic frequency interval (2 kHz to 150 kHz) is the definition of the supply conditions namely the feeding impedance; in addition, emissions in this frequency range are a mix of differential- and common-mode emissions, with prevalence of the former. It is demonstrated that supply impedance values at the EV charger connection may be highly variable depending on network loading and location of the other connected EV chargers: some scenarios of small and medium extension of the DC network are evaluated, showing peculiar frequency intervals where emissions could vary by as much as 20 dB simply as the consequence of connection and disconnection of other EVs.

articleTitle: Impact of Emission Noise and Electromagnetic Shielding on Mobile Communication Systems in Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are widely spreading in industrial fields such as logistics, surveillance, and disaster relief. UAVs are usually controlled through remote controllers, but the transmission range is limited to a few kilometers. To expand their flight area, industrial UAVs use mobile communication systems. Mobile communication systems, such as long-term evolution (LTE) and 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> generation (5G), are sensitive to electromagnetic interference since 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> generation partnership project (3GPP) defined the receiver sensitivity of mobile communication systems to operate correctly even at low power. The electromagnetic (EM) environment is complex since various electric modules are densely mounted inside UAVs. Therefore, UAVs need evaluation and countermeasures for electromagnetic interference to operate safely above a populated area. This paper shows the evaluation of emission noise from UAVs and the effect of EM shielding by their chassis. In the case of the test UAV, emission noise degraded the receiver sensitivity of the LTE communication system by 30 dB, and the EM shielding degraded the sensitivity by 18 dB in the 800-MHz band. Emission noise and EM shielding significantly impact the wireless performance of UAVs.

articleTitle: Statistical Inference of Electric Fields in Lossy Reverberating Environments Subject to High Intensity Radiated Field and Direct Current Injection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This contribution infers the statistical field properties in lossy electrically large test objects subject to radiated and conducted immunity tests on a simulative and experimental basis. By the example of High Intensity Radiated Field (HIRF) and Direct Current Injection (DCI) the electric field data in a generic test object are calculated and distribution functions are fitted to the sample data. Via statistical hypothesis testing the similarity of theoretical and sample distributions obtained for HIRF and DCI excitations is analyzed. HIRF and DCI sample distributions are compared for simulation results as well as for additional measurements. It is shown that the obtained distributions for HIRF and DCI in general are in accordance with those predicted by reverberation chamber theory, but more general two-parameter distributions lead to an improved fit in lossy reverberating environments. Despite the same underlying distributions, their parameters for certain configurations differ for HIRF and DCI, indicating the different excitation characteristics of both test methods.

articleTitle: Investigation of Guard Trace Utilization for EM Coupling Reduction Between Closely-Spaced Microstrip Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents an electromagnetic (EM) decoupling technique for a closely-spaced microstrip patch antenna array. To reduce the EM coupling, a guard trace, a structure consisting of a microstrip line with grounded vias, is inserted between the antenna patches. Parametric studies are carried out to determine the parameters of guard-trace, including the number of vias and the via diameter. To investigate the effectiveness of guard trace utilization for EM coupling reduction, a two-elements microstrip patch antenna array with a guard trace is designed to work at the frequency of 2.4 GHz. While to verify the design, the prototype of microstrip patch antenna array is realized and characterized. Measurement results indicate a coupling reduction of about 5 dB can be achieved when a 4-vias guard trace with the via diameter of 1 mm is inserted between the antenna patches separated by an edge-to-edge distance of 4 mm. Since the strongest coupling reduction occurs at very close distances between antennas, implementation of the proposed concept to massive elements antenna arrays is potential to reduce their footprint.

articleTitle: Frequency hopping signals tracking and sorting algorithm for military radio networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In this article we present a frequency hopping tracking and sorting algorithm developed from experimentally measured data and customized for military very high frequency hopping radio networks. We have exploited the capabilities of a real-time spectrum analyzer to retrieve the experimental data that was used to drive the algorithm development. In the first part, the algorithm development is detailed and in the second part the tracking and sorting capabilities of the algorithm were tested in different experimental scenarios. The algorithm tracking accuracy remains above 92% for all evaluated hoping rates and signal to noise ratio conditions. The sorting capability of the algorithm was testes over the air in a real deployment scenario, achieving a sorting accuracy as high as 91%. Present results suggest the possibility of using this algorithm to implement operational systems capable of performing real-time signal reconnaissance of military frequency hopping radio networks.

articleTitle: Bus Electrocardiogram: Vulnerability of SoC-FPGA Internal AXI Bus to Electromagnetic Side-Channel Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This article demonstrates a confidential data vulnerability in integrated circuits, especially in System-on-Chip (SoC)-field programmable gate array (FPGA). We demonstrate that the electromagnetic (EM) emanations of internal Advanced eXtensible Interface (AXI) standard data bus are exploitable. Electromagnetic pulses recorded by a near-field probe in the vicinity of such data bus can be mapped to the underlying data flux, just as an electrocardiogram (ECG) would map the heart activity and blood circulation. This vulnerability is demonstrated by spying on the EM emanations caused by internal bus while MNIST handwritten digit images are sent through them. The transmitted MNIST data are found to be framed by pre-amble and post-amble signals enabling the detection of transmitted data themselves. Data (images, in this paper) are then reconstituted by using a simple algorithm.

articleTitle: Broadband 3D Modeling and Simulation of DC-Biased SMT Ferrite Beads for EMI Filters
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Electromagnetic interference (EMI) within electronic based systems (EBS) became a fundamental issue that requires dedicated countermeasures e.g. filter structures to avoid unintended system behavior. The sefilters comprise several components including surface-mounted(SMT) devices to suppress unwanted electromagnetic emissions. However, these devices change their behavior due to dispersion-and saturation-effects (ferroelectric-and ferromagnetic-effect), hence applying a DC bias current might lead to a significantly different behavior than intended. The presented methodology allows a broadband characterization of ferrite core materials used in SMT ferrite bead to predict the impact of dispersion-and saturation-effects on impedance behavior of device. The proposed modeling strategy is based on the Kramers-Kronig relation, vector network analyzer (VNA) measurements, and full-wave finite element simulations.The Extracted Material Models are validated for a frequency range from 100 kHz - 1 GHz and DC bias current levels up to 5A.

articleTitle: Circuit Modeling of Fast Ethernet Signal for EMC and SI Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The 100BASE-TX Fast Ethernet is the most widely adopted standard in residential sector today. This standard requires the signal generated by the physical layer to be encoded with a Multi-Level Transmit (MLT)-3 modulation, which shifts the spectrum energy to low frequencies. Improper design of the Fast Ethernet system causes Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) and Signal Integrity (SI) related issues that occur in real-world applications, yet an efficient circuit model for MLT-3 signal generation, which is crucial for system EMC and SI performance evaluation, is not available in the literature. This paper fills this gap by presenting a circuit model that simulates the behavior of the physical layer for Fast Ethernet applications. By tuning the sampling frequency parameter of the circuit and adding an RC filter, the circuit model mimics the time-domain and frequency-domain characteristics of a measured MLT-3 signal, allowing to effectively address the testing and optimization of EMC and SI issues in Fast Ethernet systems.

articleTitle: Measuring Receiver Benchmark for Conducted and Radiated Emissions Testing in Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper compares the measurement results obtained from three different implementations of measuring receivers regarding spectral level accuracy. The objective is to validate the suitability of direct sampling electromagnetic emissions measurements with respect to those delivered by a high-end EMI receiver in frequency swept and FFT modes. The experimental setups follow the verification methods described in the ECSS-E-ST-20-07C Rev.2 standard to set realistic and reproducible conditions. Between 50 kHz and 100 MHz, common mode and differential mode currents are measured when multi-sine excitation signals with controlled amplitude profiles are used as references. Subsequently, conducted and radiated emissions tests are run to investigate the correlation between measurements with the different receivers. The instruments used are a low-cost USB digitiser Picoscope PS5444D, a high-performance benchtop oscilloscope R&S RTO6 and the R&S ESW44 full-compliant EMI test receiver. The analysis concludes that the emissions measurements performed with the direct sampling approach are excellent for the intended application, exhibiting an accuracy comparable to the dedicated EMI test receiver and a well-adequate dynamic range and noise level.

articleTitle: Signal Integrity Design of PCB Transmission Paths using a Decision Tree Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The demand for decreasing physical dimensions and switching times in high speed systems causes signal distortions due to reflections on transmission paths. The task of a designer consists of finding an appropriate physical parameter set in order to maintain proper signal quality. This can be challenging for complex systems with a high dimension of the parameter space. An AI-assisted design system is proposed to support the designer for speeding up SI conform circuit design. A decision tree approach is introduced for an assessment of a DDR3 daisy chain topology. For this purpose, different design configurations are used to generate various data sets. Output waveforms from SI simulations are evaluated and SI conform signal curves are predicted based on selected features. Further shortening of switching times also leads to higher slew rates. Therefore, among other features for training the AI modules, the slew rate is also used as an important feature. Furthermore, the implemented AI models trained by a specific set of SI simulations are tested with regard to their applicability to related DDR3 configurations, which were not known during the training process (transfer learning). The proposed approach provides a model, which allows the designer to understand the suggested predictions (explainable AI).

articleTitle: Direct Current Mode Stirred –Susceptibility Testing Results of a small EUT and Comparison to RC and SAC Results
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The Direct Current Mode Stirred method (DCMS) has already been outlined in several papers before and is described shortly in here for consistency. In principle it combines the method of Direct Current Injection (DCI), which injects currents on surfaces of test objects and the Reverberation Chamber (RC) test method for Radio Frequency (RF) susceptibility testing. The motivation is mainly driven by the high efficiency of these two methods and the therefore resulting high field levels, which can be generated by moderate RF power requirements. The major drawback of the RC, with the lowest usable frequency (LUF) which ranges typically at some hundred megahertz, can be shifted towards very low frequencies when being combined with DCI. The DCI (or HLDD, High level Direct Drive) method is very effective in the low frequency range and is limited at higher frequencies, due to RF adaption and strong radiation. The highest usable frequency lies typically at some hundred megahertz. A combination of these two methods could allow much more effective susceptibility testing than with standard antenna radiation techniques.This paper outlines the measurement results, which were gained in four different RCs for the DCMS method with a small Equipment Under Test (EUT). Additionally, at some testing locations, IEC or MIL standard conformal susceptibility tests in a RC and Semi Anechoic Chamber (SAC) were done. Furthermore, it compares the results, which were gained in the four different RCs of different size and also shows the differences to the IEC or MIL standard conformal test results. A conversion factor of the DCMS method to IEC or MIL standard conformal susceptibility tests is foreseen in the future but is not part of this paper.

articleTitle: Extracting High Speed Refresh Current for DDR5 Module based on Network Parameter Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In this paper, we proposed an extracting method of immeasurable chip-level current based on printed circuit board network parameters and the measurement data on the surface mount device component. To get the accurate current consumed in chip, that is chip-level current, the interposer was designed and applied. And the power distribution network of the chip was modeled by measuring S-parameters and the power distribution network for printed circuit board, and the package were modeled using the numerical analysis tool. The transient simulation was performed to verify the proposed method. The verification was completed at the simulation level by applying the proposed method to the data obtained from the simulation results. As a result, the chip-level current was extracted by applying the method to the actual dynamic random access memory on the 2 rank by 4 registered dual-in line module sample. This method can be applied to all memory products that can mount an interposer.

articleTitle: Investigating the CM Noise Generated by Different Configurations of Multiple Forward Converters
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Switched-mode power supplies (SMPSs) are utilized with fast-switching wide band-gap devices that operate at switching frequencies in the hundreds of kHz range and very short switching time. As a result of the wide spectrum, electromagnetic interference (EMI) is a critical issue for SMPS. The size and weight of power line filters can decrease as the frequency increases. Higher frequency, on the other hand, increases the generated EMI noise, so the size and cost of the required EMI filters are difficult to assess due to conflicting requirements for high power density applications. Conversely, as parasitic effects become more dominant in the high frequency range, increasing switching frequency may result in higher levels of high frequency EMI noise. Connecting multiple converters in the input and output ports have demonstrated their effectiveness in reducing EMI, such as interleaving, which connects in parallel for both ports. However, other configurations based on series and parallel at the two ports have not been addressed. This paper will address three different configurations for connecting two forward converters in comparison with single forward converter. Based on the simulation of three configurations, this paper shows that the CM noise is highly influenced by the input node parasitics.

articleTitle: Analysis Method for Magnetic Field Strength on On-Board Antenna due to Inverter Common-Mode Noise at Whole Train Level
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In order to reduce malfunctions of on-board equipment due to noise generated by inverters in rolling stock, a method for analyzing magnetic field noise received by on-board equipment is required. To achieve this, it was necessary to identify the main currents among the noise currents flowing near the onboard antenna and to construct a model that takes into account the phase of those currents. In the work reported here, we identified that the imbalance between the left and right rail currents contributes to the magnetic field noise and constructed a vehicle-level analysis model that includes these noise currents. The analysis confirmed that the model can represent the variation of noise fluctuation for each frame structure around the on-board equipment up to 2 MHz.

articleTitle: Survey of RF Electromagnetic Field Exposure in a Public Health Research Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Healthcare environments are immersed in the intensive development of 5G mobile communications, involving a significant increase in the mobile traffic area capacity and density of sources of electromagnetic radiation in a very wide mixture of electric fields of different frequencies. This paper analyzes the signals of different wireless communications systems in 10 locations at a Public Health Spanish reference Research Center, in Madrid, ISCIII, at an outdoor environment. The experimental values of the electric field, obtained with an EME Spy 200 MVG dosimeter were performed with the same conditions and compared for the ten locations between two measurement campaigns. The tree locations with most important exposure to communications systems (Down Links) were selected and analyzed the evolution of results in order to verify regulations concerning the safety of patients, general public and workers in health environment, who often are exposed to the electromagnetic field (EMF) emitted by wireless telecommunications systems with different features and intensities and changes in the structure of radiocommunication services and their physical infrastructure. Most important exposure to LTE B13 (DL), LTE B4 (DL) and LTE B7 (DL) cause relatively higher E/m values, all of them higher levels in the second campaign and in any case do not exceed the ICNIRP reference levels, which remains significantly low.

articleTitle: Generalized Cylindrical Mode Filtered Site VSWR for Above 18 GHz EMC Site Evaluation Using Compressed Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Site Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (SVSWR), as defined in CISPR 16-1-4 or ANSI C63.25.1, has been established as the de facto standard for evaluating the performance of an EMC test site from 1 GHz to 18 GHz. There is a growing need to develop a similar standard for the 18 GHz to 40 GHz range. Researches have shown that the existing methods below 18 GHz do not extrapolate well to the higher frequencies. A new method based cylindrical mode filtered SVSWR was introduced recently to address the limitations of the previous methods. In the mode filtered method, an omni-directional transmit antenna is placed at the edge of the quiet zone, and a single cut antenna pattern is measured. The data is then processed, transformed into cylindrical modes, and then filtered to obtain the "clean" reference pattern. The Mode Filtered SVSWR implementation had previously relied on equally-spaced angular sampling to compute the Cylindrical Mode Coefficients (CMCs) via Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). In this paper, we expand the methodology to a much more general case to allow undersampled data (below the Nyquist rate) and on an unequally-spaced abscissa. CMCs are then accurately computed using the Compressed Sensing (CS) algorithm. Measured results show the validity and effectiveness of the new algorithm.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Effect of Deviated Modulating Signal Characteristics on the Susceptibility of a Small Medical Device
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: A variety of modulation techniques using various signal characteristics are used by the telecommunication industry in real-life applications. Despite this, the radiated immunity test based on the IEC 61000-4-3 only modulates in amplitude the carrier signal using a 1 kHz sine wave at 80% depth. In this study, we performed the radiated immunity test on a miniaturized device with biomedical applications using deviated signal-modulating characteristics than those mentioned in the IEC 61000-4-3. The results show that it is important to carry out an adequate risk analysis of the equipment under test (EUT) considering its unique functional characteristics before resorting to just the modulating frequency mentioned in the standards.

articleTitle: High Temperature Accelerated Ageing Influence on the Conducted Immunity Modelling of the Commonly Used Voltage Regulator ICs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper aims to develop and compare the integrated circuit conducted immunity (ICIM-CI) models of two different voltage regulator ICs with similar functionality (i.e., UA78L05 and L78L05) under the combined influence of two different electrical overstress (i.e., 9 and 12 V) and high temperature (i.e., 70–110 °C) stresses ageing conditions for a total stress duration of 950 hours. Step-stress accelerated degradation tests (SSADT) are performed on two samples of UA78L05 (i.e., T1 and T2) and L78L08 (i.e., S1 and S2) manufactured by Texas Instrument and STMicroelectronics, respectively. Direct power injection (DPI) test was conducted in nominal conditions (i.e., 7.5 V and 25 °C) on these selected ICs according to IEC 62132-4 standard before and after the accelerated ageing test. For the studied cases, it was found that the passive distribution network (PDN) models extracted before and after ageing test for the ICIM-CI model of UA78L05 and L78L05 remained unaffected. However, the ageing process affected the internal behavioral (IB) block of the ICIM-CI model significantly due to noticeable reduction in the conducted immunity level characterized by the extracted IB look-up table data in terms of power transmitted and frequency. Both fresh and aged samples of L78L05 demonstrated higher conducted immunity profile compared to those of UA78L05.

articleTitle: Emission from Wireless Power Transfer of Electrical Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: As a new application within the wireless power transfer (WPT) technique, stationary charging of vehicles is introduced. The technique goes under the concept wireless power transfer to electric vehicles (WPT-EV). For this purpose, the frequency band 75–90 kHz can be used with means of a transmitting coil located in the ground that transfers energy to a receiving coil in the vehicle floor. There is a risk that the WPT-EV may cause electromagnetic interference in radio communication systems. To gain knowledge of the emission levels originated from the WPT-EV station and the character of the radiated signals, measurement has been conducted. In this paper the measurement results are presented for the frequency band 9 kHz to 30 MHz at 3 and 10 m.It is shown that the WPT-EV is clearly generating interference in the measured frequency band. The charging frequency at 83 kHz exhibit levels between 64 and 81 dBμA/m at 3 meters and between 58 and 65 dBμA/m at 10 meter. The frequency band between 1 and 12 MHz shows a significant increase in level and harmonics from the charging frequency of 83 kHz appears in the measured frequency band.

articleTitle: Influence of Complex Magnetic Permeability on 3-D Simulation of MnZn Common-Mode Chokes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Common-mode chokes (CMC) are fundamental in electromagnetic interference (EMI) filters. 3-D simulation is becoming more and more important in recent years as it can take into account some effects that circuit modeling does not consider, such as the surrounding environment of the CMC. This paper investigates the influence of complex magnetic permeability on the 3-D simulation of a Mn-Zn CMC in its typical application frequency range (below 10 MHz). For this purpose, a simple method to extract complex permeability values by winding cores with a copper wire is applied. Then, the error in the extraction with different turn numbers is studied, and the setup to successfully perform a 3-D simulation of a Mn-Zn CMC is detailed. Finally, simulations of a commercial Mn-Zn CMC are performed up to 10 MHz to check the influence on electromagnetic simulations of complex permeability values extracted with different turn numbers.

articleTitle: Modeling and Stability Analysis of Voltage Sense Current Cancellation Active EMI Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper introduces a feedback voltage sense current compensation topology for active EMI filters (AEF), which provided good noise suppression and ensures high frequency stability. First, the performance is analyzed mathematically. Design rules for the AEF and all passive components are derived. Secondly, the filter is realized and integrated in a laboratory setup with a 400W AC/DC power supply and analyzed. Between 300 kHz and 2 MHz a reduction of EMI emission of more than 10 dB could be achieved. The measured attenuation of the AEF matches well with the theoretical expectations.

articleTitle: Single-probe Near-field Phase Retrieval using On-The-Fly Scan and Hilbert Transform
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: A novel near-field measurement method is proposed for fast phase retrieval using a single probe. The method is based on a new understanding of the on-the-fly (OTF) scan process as a spatio-temporal sampling operation of near-field responses. As a result, the near-field measurement is interpreted as a signal modulation of a source signal and a variable spatio-temporal function defined by the field responses and the motion of the probe. To retrieve the complex field responses, the Hilbert Transform (HT) is utilized for envelope and phase demodulation of signals recorded by an oscilloscope. To demonstrate the proof of concept, both numerical and experimental examples are provided with a detailed description of the method implementation. Measurement-to-measurement correlations at 125 kHz are conducted using a six-axis industry robot with multiple probes and instruments, showing its efficiency, effectiveness, and flexibility. Compared to conventional near-field measurement methods, the proposed method allows 90% reduction of measurement time and achieves a relative accuracy of phase retrieval above 96% with a simplified measurement setup, opening up new opportunities for near-field measurement applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of Cancellation Path Estimation Errors in Narrow-band Adaptive Digital Active EMI Filters
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Fast switching power electronic systems can be critical emitters of electromagnetic disturbances. For the reduction of the disturbances, active EMI filtering (AEF) promises reduced overall weight and volume compared to passive filters. Analog and digital AEF approaches are known. With help of fast and precise analog-to-digital converters, digital-to-analog converters and modern digital signal processing hardware as, e.g., field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), digital active EMI Filters (DAEFs) can realize complex filtering algorithms and reach higher frequencies than analog approaches. Until now, digital adaptive notch filters or narrow-band adaptive digital active EMI filters (NADAEFs) have been successfully applied to different applications. But for stable and successful operation, a valid estimation of the transfer function of the cancellation path is needed. In this paper, cancellation path estimation errors are investigated with regard to their impact on active EMI reduction. A transfer function model is presented and used for a detailed performance analysis in order to find critical parameters and potential for optimization.

articleTitle: Impact of Supply Voltage and Operating Point in IC PDN Modeling
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The effect of different supply voltages and operating points on the impedance characteristics of an integrated circuit is analyzed in this paper. The approach presented is based on S-parameter measurements of a simple but representative electronic circuit, a 74HC14 hex inverter IC with Schmitt trigger inputs. The impedances change significantly with different operating points and the use of decoupling capacitors, but only slightly with different supply voltages. These measurement results are compared to a simple PDN model to illustrate future requirements for more accurate SPICE-level modeling of an IC’s passive distribution network with respect to the IEC 62433 standard.

articleTitle: An Investigation of Lithium-ion Battery Induced Near Field Electromagnetic Interference in Wearable Audio Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Recently, lightweight, compact, and imperceptible wearable products push the interaction between consumers and electronic devices to a new level. However, they also pose more challenges in terms of EMC design. On one hand, it is also necessary to change the methods of coupling path analysis from large 2D-like circuit boards design to full 3D stacking since the predictable interferences have changed from traditional PCBs, high-speed/high-power IC, to various sensors and components with high sensitivity. Furthermore, in extreme compact stacking conditions, it is difficult to predict the spatial distribution of electric and magnetic fields and how they may affect various devices. On the other hand, the impact of electromagnetic interference on sensitive devices extends beyond the simple degradation of electronic performance. It directly impacts the user's perception and experience, which puts higher demands on the product level EMC design.In this paper, the TWS (True Wireless Stereo) earbuds are used as an example to illustrate an interdisciplinary electromagnetic analysis method that encompasses the fields of electromagnetics, battery design, acoustics, RF, and baseband. Our study analyzes the electromagnetic radiation emitted by batteries, and proposes high-precision models of batteries and high-sensitivity speakers. In order to verify its accuracy, we have compared the simulation and actual measurement and we have also proposed a new anti-interference battery to address these issues.

articleTitle: An Assessment of Multilevel Converters Submodules EMI Emissions Considering Three Configurations Including Parasitic Parameters
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: With the expanding use of modular multilevel converters in power installations it became more important to lower the total conducted emissions. One of the most important key factors in controlling electromagnetic interference emissions is the type of submodules used and the utilized switches. This paper compares three well-known submodules which are half bridge, full bridge and double-clamped half bridge effect on the electromagnetic interference emissions. For making the model more accurate the parasitic components were included in all the circuits Additionally, the same configurations are carried out and compared under two switches which are insulated gate bipolar transistors and metal oxide semiconductor field effect transistors operating at two different switching frequencies. The results were obtained by a simulation in a Matlab/Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Analysis of Multi-Filter EMI Mitigation for Weight and Volume Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: All-electric aircraft (AEA) require an increased number of power converters, making it potentially more susceptible to electromagnetic interference (EMI). This paper explores the volume optimization of passive EMI filters for a multi-converter system. It explores the distribution of filtering demand between localized and centralized solutions. The bulkiest filtering elements are directed to localized filters. While smaller components are centralized. This leads to a reduction in localized volume, as space availability is limited in aerospace applications, specially in smaller subsystems. The performance of each solution is presented and compared.

articleTitle: Harmonic Distortion Reference Structure for Contact Induced Harmonics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Today's mobile device designs make extensive use of electrical interconnects, ESD protection and magnetic materials, all of which can be potential sources of interference due to harmonic distortion from strong TX signals due to non-linearities. Harmonic generation, particularly from contacts, is highly variable. Therefore, a stable and controllable harmonic reference source is required for nonlinear interference analysis in such devices. This paper proposes a harmonic reference source based on the Schottky diode. It produces consistent and adjustable distortion. Simulations agree very well with measurements up to the low gigahertz range. This allows validation and comparison in difficult environments such as contact harmonics in mobile phones.

articleTitle: Comparison between segregation and filtering using a black-box inverter model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Electrification of aircraft propulsion increases embedded power electronics and leads to reconsider specification and integration logic of power electronics systems. At the same time, aeronautics constraints, such as weight and volume, requires to wisely define segregation rules and avoid additional filters. These two solutions are compared through a practical case. To do so, a power chain is modelled and experimentally validated over different network impedances. Segregation and filtering values are defined to comply with victim susceptibility limit. At the end, the solutions are compared over different criteria.

articleTitle: Intrusion Detection and Shielding Measurements using Signals of Opportunity
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Shielding effectiveness measurements of big structures such as information security centers, safe rooms, and nuclear power plants can be challenging because they can be time-consuming, costly, and difficult to apply. Since the shielding effectiveness is a critical parameter for such structures, the measurements are needed to be repeated periodically, especially for TEMPEST shielded rooms. This study proposes an improvement to shielding effectiveness measurements utilizing signals of opportunity. In this technique, different from the classical measurement methods, the strengths of already-existing-signals in the given environment are used instead of purposely generating them with dedicated hardware. By taking the differences between the measurements performed inside and outside a cabinet, or a room, a quick estimation can be made for the shielding effectiveness. The technique can be applied to evaluate the deterioration of shielding or as a watchdog for intrusion detection. The paper concluded with a discussion of the pros and cons of the method.

articleTitle: Passive Cell Balancing Impact On Injection Levels During Direct Power injection on Battery Cell Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: When it comes to the electromagnetic interference (EMI) immunity of a Battery Management Systems (BMS) or more specifically Battery Cell Controllers Integrated Circuit (BCC IC), Printed Circuit Board (PCB) traces and external components (ECs) arrangement are crucial. The impedance presented by the BCC IC is also a key factor. In fact, such impedance is greatly altered by the cell balancing function of the BCC IC. More specifically, the integrated passive cell balancing function in most commercially available BCC ICs greatly reduces the impedance presented by the BCC IC. This work aims at investigating the impact of different passive cell balancing approaches on the immunity level of the BCC IC. Then a new BCC IC architecture is presented that not only reduces the number of ECs but also allows the passive cell balancing to have the most impact on the immunity of IC, i.e. the injections levels during DPI tests. Thus, the IC can maintain a high voltage measurement accuracy in noisy environments.

articleTitle: SPICE-based model validation for 1200V AcepackTM Drive traction power module
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The main aim of this work is to present the electrical analysis of the Acepack<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sup> Drive housing an half bridge configuration with 8 SiC MOSFET per switch. The analysis is performed by means of SPICE model simulation setup and the results have been compared with experimental measurements. The experimentally validated simulation model can be exploited to investigate the electrical behavior of the power module in a wider operating range, by considering different working conditions and applications.

articleTitle: Comparison Results of the Conducted and Radiated Measurements of a Radio Device Performed under Temperature Extreme Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents a comparison of the measurement results of spectrum and power parameters of radio equipment under extreme temperature conditions measured in a conducted and radiated manner. Equipment under test (EUT) had a built-in antenna. For conducted tests in a climate chamber, EUT had to be modified with temporary Radiated measurements performed in the Fully Anechoic Room with radio equipment placed in a special mini-climate chamber designed in a way that does not affect the propagation of radio waves connector. The goal of this work is to investigate whether such modification affects the radio parameters of the radio module.

articleTitle: An Experimental Study of the Effects of Internal Loading on the Measured Shielding Effectiveness of Printed Circuit Board Shields
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The measurement of shielding effectiveness of printed circuit board shields can be undertaken with the shields connected to a measurement jig installed in a reverberation chamber. The internal loading of the printed circuit board shield is not normally accounted for in Shielding Effectiveness measurements. The measurement jig used in this paper has internal loading in the form of a stripline that is used to measure the energy coupled into the shield. Normally this stripline is terminated in matched loads. In this paper we illustrate the effects on the measured Shielding Effectiveness of the printed circuit board shield of changing the terminations of the internal stripline and of the addition of extra absorbing material into the shield.

articleTitle: Prediction of automotive radiated emission using machine learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: A machine learning model that predicts automotive radiated emissions under CISPR25 conditions from near-field noise is developed as a neural network. The model demonstrates a versatile performance that predicts radiated emissions from samples other than those used in the learning phase. It shows low dependency of predictive performance on the neural network’s hyperparameters.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation Result of Preliminary Measurement for In-Situ Test Method in CISPR 37
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Since 2018, IEC/CISPR SCB (International Special Committee on Radio Interference, Subcommittee B) has started developing an in-situ measurement method (CISPR 37) as a test method for large, high-power equipment that is difficult to measure at the conventional test site, such as semi anechoic chamber [1]. In the discussion, the appropriate method of determining the measurement points has become an important issue. For compliance testing, it is not easy to choose measurement points in a reference distance to obtain maximum radiated emissions.In this paper, we propose the application of preliminary measurement specified in CISPR 16-2-3 [2] to determine the final measurement points, and evaluated the effectiveness experimentally. It is different from the accurate prediction technique from the near field to the far field in the electromagnetic field theory.

articleTitle: Modal Analysis of Bulk Current Injection Tests Involving Multiwire Harnesses
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Modal analysis is a powerful tool for noise identification and predicting noise voltages and currents. For this reason, it can be adopted to infer the outcomes of bulk current injection (BCI) tests on multi-wire bundles for conducted susceptibility verifications through a suitable model of mode conversion. Moreover, upper and lower limits for terminal voltages and currents can be computed through statistical investigations, allowing to identify best- and worst-case scenarios for the considered test campaign. In this framework, a decoupled modal-domain analysis is designed and presented for predicting the results of conducted susceptibility tests involving BCI probes. In particular, this work aims to improve the accuracy of the modal analysis by introducing an intermediate step in the procedure, while ensuring efficiency compared to the traditional method working in the physical domain.

articleTitle: Improved System for Measuring Contact Induced Harmonics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Portable wireless devices cannot avoid electrical contact due to assembly and maintenance requirements. In this paper, an improved test system is proposed for systematic investigation of harmonic distortion induced by metal to metal contacts. The system supports harmonic distortion measurements, DC resistance measurements, fine control of contact force or contraction and automatic re-mating for statistical purposes. In this regard, forward and reflected harmonic signals are measured and ultrasonic vibration is applied to cure contacts. A novel sample holder structure is designed and fabricated as a test vehicle for the measurements.

articleTitle: Coupling Path to Attached Cables in an Arbitrary Flyback Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Common mode current coupling to cables from power converter PCBs are commonly known to cause radiated emission problems at lower frequencies. This paper identifies the coupling path using a coupling coefficient method by the use of full wave simulation and successfully identified and reduces emissions at specific frequencies.

articleTitle: Assessment of the Effect of a Test Setup on the Input Impedance Measurement of Cables
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper aims at a new assessment to investigate the effect of a test setup on the input impedance of cables. The test setup includes a vertical reference plane connected to a horizontal ground plane. A connector is screwed into the vertical plane. The connector from one side is connected to a measurement device and from another side, it is connected to a cable. To assess the effect of the setup on connectors, the SMA connector and the end-launch connector are connected to the setup separately and the input impedance of the setup is measured. The results suggest that the vertical plane and the connectors have a significant impact on the test setup up to 6 GHz. This impact can be observed even by adding a 1m wire to the test setup.

articleTitle: Correlation of Electromagnetic Interference in Inverter and Radio Disturbance on Assessment of Component and Battery Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Electromagnetic interference generated by the power modules of the inverter in battery electric vehicles causes degradation of the radio broadcasting performance in vehicle antennas. The discrepancies in the input impedance from the inverter between the assessment of the component and vehicle could affect the common mode current. In this study, the correlation between the conducted currents in both the components and the battery electric vehicle was evaluated. In addition, the relationships between the electromagnetic interference in the inverter, the drive shafts, and the interference voltage at the radio antenna cable are also examined. The correlations were investigated experimentally and computationally using the common mode ferrite core and Y capacitance for frequencies ranging from 150 kHz to 30 MHz. The result showed that the common mode current in the vehicle is significant high at 1.2 MHz with only Y capacitance installed in the vehicle (no ferrite core), which was attributable to a lower input impedance from the inverter in the vehicle. In addition, our study demonstrated the strong correlations between the common mode current, the electric field at the drive shaft, and the voltage at the radio antenna. The investigation results provide suggestions for appropriate suppression for the electromagnetic interference at the early design stage of the component, taking into account the gap of the impedance characteristic in the vehicle.

articleTitle: Usage of Ansys in Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) Simulations for Automotive Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The article presents a methodology for performing Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) simulations using the Ansys software tools. As an example, one of Aptiv's production products, an automotive camera was utilized. The simulation studies incorporated a model of the ESD gun compliant with automotive standards and a simulation model of a camera in series production. The PCB model, electrical component models and the connector model were included. The article highlights some good practices regarding ESD simulations. Attention is also paid to some good practices in the design of PCB ESD protection.

articleTitle: Computational Electromagnetics of Reverberation Chambers and an Open Coaxial Return Rig
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The combination of Direct Current Injection (DCI) with the resonant properties of a Reverberation Chamber (RC) leads to the Direct Current Mode Stirred (DCMS) test method, which aims at fulfilling the high field level requirements for electromagnetic susceptibility testing according to RTCA DO-160 over the whole frequency range of 10 kHz up to 18 GHz. The major advantage of DCMS is the possibility to conduct EMC qualification at a single test site without the need to relocate the EUT for different frequencies under test. However, in order to establish DCMS as a standardized EMC test method, a conversion method between injected power and equivalent external field strength is required. For corroborating a potential conversion theorem in the future, a measurement campaign at several RC test sites is conducted. The campaign is supported by numerical simulations to provide reliable models of the investigated test environments. This paper focuses on the numerical simulation approach. It shows the designed models for the reverberation chambers and the EUT. Furthermore the difficulties of the modeling process are discussed. The results obtained with the numerical simulations are directly compared to the measurement results.

articleTitle: Observations of radiated and conducted emissions from an Electric Plane charging station
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The paper reports a set of radiated and conducted emissions recorded at an electric airplane's charging station located in Sweden. The measurement exercise undertaken shows the existence of supraharmonic frequency components exceeding the IEC 61000-2-2 limits in the frequency range 129 to 147 kHz. These components are visible in the radiated emissions recorded at the test site as well. Observations of the measured common mode current offer a possible explanation for the radiated magnetic field recorded at the test site in the sub 150 kHz band.

articleTitle: New Evaluation Concept for Electromagnetic Interference of HVDC Cables to neighboring Buried Pipelines
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The demand of energy transition rises worldwide permanently. New HVDC corridors in Germany are mainly constructed to be realized as high voltage DC cables over hundreds of kilometers and the cases of close proximity of HVDC cables to buried metallic pipelines become more frequent. Although several standards and guidelines cover the analysis and mitigation issues of AC interference between high voltage lines (or even AC cables) to the buried metallic infrastructures, there is still a big lack of guidelines, how to deal with electromagnetic interference between DC cables and neighboring buried pipelines. Considering AC guidelines for evaluating DC interference causes a large field of non-solved discussions, as there are significant response differences between AC and DC interference. Especially the interpretation of calculated induced voltage on the pipelines due to neighboring HVDC cables is the major difficulty of the topic. In this paper a new concept for evaluating the electromagnetic interference and the consequences between DC cables and buried pipelines is developed and evaluated within an example of a new long DC cable corridor in Germany (A-Nord).

articleTitle: Mitigating Common-Mode Noise in the Totem Pole Bridgeless PFC Using Balance Boost Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The global energy system is facing several challenges and risks that will greatly affect energy production and consumption in the future. One potential solution to these problems is the utilization of power electronics converter. In these days, the Totem Pole Bridgeless (TPB) Power Factor Correction (PFC) converter attracts extended interest with development of SiC-MOSFET. Requiring only a few components, it has the advantage of combining very good efficiency with active management of the inrush current when thyristors or silicon-controlled rectifiers (SCRs) replace the diodes in the low frequency arm. Nevertheless, the common mode (CM) noise (generated by high dV/dt of SiC-MOSFET coupled with the parasitic capacitances) remains the major challenge of the architecture "Totem Pole". To overcome this problem, this paper introduces a technique based on a balance condition of the Wheatstone bridge to nullify conducted noise (150 kHz – 30 MHz) in CM. Furthermore, this study conducts a more in-depth examination of the effect of incorporating an EMI filer on the reduction of CM noise when balance technique is applied to the TPB-PFC converter.

articleTitle: A PCB Based High Resistance GHz Bandwidth Voltage Pick Up for Detecting Switching Voltage
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The sub-nanosecond switching of GaN transistors at high voltages challenges existing methods of transient voltage measurement. A novel printed circuit board based implementation of a capacitively compensated resistive divider is presented in this paper. The geometry balances capacitive coupling to the high voltage side with capacitive coupling to ground and longitudinal capacitances along the resistors by symmetry. Using five 2 watt resistors a 3 GHz bandwidth is achieved at 5 KOhm. An equivalent circuit derived from the geometry and the full-wave model are validated by measurements.

articleTitle: Modeling a GaN Transistor and its Impact on Conducted Emission up to 300 MHz
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Accurate transistor models in the wide frequency range are essential for the prediction of electromagnetic interference. This paper investigates the applicability of a silicon power MOSFET behavioral model to GaN transistors and shows which parameters are important for modeling high-frequency emissions. In the tested case we show that GaN modeling is feasible up to 300 MHz using datasheet information and a single measurement. In addition, a simplified power MOSFET model is proposed that requires only three lumped element values and an ideal diode. We also investigate the impact of the layout by 3D simulations, the impact of two DC voltage levels, and we compare the simulated results to measurements.

articleTitle: Configurable Resonant and Broadband Magnetic Near-Field Probe
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: A magnetic field probe is described which can be configured to be either broadband or resonant. The designs shown range in size from 4 x 4 mm to 0.8 x 0.5 mm loop size and can be configured to be resonant from 600 MHz to 2700 MHz. The design is based on a 4-layer PCB. When configured as a resonant probe, the sensitivity is approximately 12 dB better than a wideband configuration of the same size. The unwanted E-field rejection is also 18.5 dB. The effect of design choices on the Q-factor is discussed.

articleTitle: A Method to Determine the Permittivity of Anisotropic Thin Sheet Absorber Materials
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Thin sheet EMC suppression material is often manufactured in multiple layers. These artificial materials can be made by mixing metal flakes into polymers. This leads to anisotropic behavior in the electromagnetic properties of the material. This paper presents a new method for determining the anisotropic behavior of magneto-dielectric thin film materials, focusing on a measurement of both in-plane and normal-to-plane permittivity. In this procedure, the in-plane permittivity and permeability are measured using the well-known material characterization technique, and then the normal to plane permittivity is measured using the proposed technique. This method determines the value of the dielectric constant using a simple microstrip line structure. Simulation and measurement are used to verify the validity of the method.

articleTitle: Choice of STFT and WT Parameters for Monitoring of EMI in Track Circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The article considers the problem of the correct choice of the parameters of the short-time Fourier transform and the continuous wavelet transform to ensure monitoring of electromagnetic interference in rails in order to ensure the electromagnetic compatibility of traction current with track circuits. The problem of correct choice of parameters for the time-frequency analysis of currents in track circuits lies in the strict requirements of the standards for the accuracy of measuring the magnitude, frequency, and duration of disturbances, as well as in the specifics of the measured current parameters and in restrictions inherent in the short-time Fourier transform and continuous wavelet transforms on the accuracy of measuring harmonic parameters. The specificity of currents in rails is associated with a large dynamic range of harmonics, a wide frequency range and the proximity of harmonics in the spectrum to each other, which makes it difficult to distinguish weak harmonics against the background of more powerful ones, as well as in the non-periodic and random nature of current. The paper considers the technology of the correct choice of parameters of the short-time Fourier transform and the continuous wavelet transforms. The results of the work were approved during testing of new types of trains.

articleTitle: Monte Carlo Simulation of a Physical Random Unintentional Radiator as a Basis for Statistics in Fully Anechoic Room Measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Current discussions of the applicability of classical standard models to calculate limit values for emission measurements in fully and semi anechoic chambers for frequencies above 1 GHz lead to a high interest to efficiently model unintentional random radiators at high frequencies. Since the radiation pattern of such sources is inherently very inhomogeneous, a high impact on the measurement procedures used in semi and fully anechoic chambers is expected. To quantify this impact, a Monte Carlo model of a physical random radiator is used. The generated radiation patterns are analyzed to represent typical test scenarios. The simulated test results are then evaluated statistically to add quantitative data to the discussion, whether standard test procedures are sufficient at high frequencies or not.

articleTitle: Rician K Factor Tuning for 5G Channel Emulation in Different Typologies of Reverberation Chambers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Reverberation chambers usually exhibit low values of the Rician k factor; this means that the stirred component of the electromagnetic field is dominant with respect to the unstirred one. To increase this parameter in order to emulate propagation environments for 5G telecommunication systems, usually lossy elements are added into the chamber. In this way, the strength of the field inside the cavity decreases and more amplification of the signal is needed. This paper shows how to increase the Rician k factor by selecting a subset of electromagnetic configurations without the insertion of dissipative material. Successful results were obtained using different typologies of stirring techniques, multiple monopole source stirring, rotating paddles mechanical stirring, and oscillating wall stirring.

articleTitle: Analysis and Modelling of a Ring Core Inductor under Saturation Effect
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This work presents an analytical model for ring-core inductors that accounts for the effect of saturation of the soft magnetic material that makes up the core. The model has been formulated in terms of the physical and geometrical properties of the coil that affect the magnetization of the material, and was obtained under certain hypotheses related to the nature of ferromagnetic materials. An heuristic algorithm has been used to determine the value of the parameters of the model to account for real performance of two hanmade inductors manufactured to validate the proposed method. This method intends to be first step towards the development of a tool for the design and optimization of inductors, transformers and common mode chokes.

articleTitle: A Time-Domain Model of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces Through the Fast Inversion of the Laplace Transform
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) technology has gained a growing interest in both academia and industry given its capability to provide more flexible and controllable wireless propagation channels. RISs typically consist of inexpensive scattering elements (i.e., unit cells), which are spaced at sub-wavelength distances, and their characterization is mainly performed in the frequency domain. The aim of this work is to present a novel time-domain modeling approach for RISs, which is based on an inverse Laplace transform and allows to overcome some of the limitations of direct time domain analyses. In particular, since propagation delays between transmitters, RIS, and receivers are important and need to be accurately reproduced, a dedicated version of the Fast Inversion of the Laplace Transform (FILT) is presented and is found to guarantee accurate time-domain representation, while preserving the causality of the system response. In contrast to conventional time-stepping methods, the presented modeling technique is stable and allows to calculate the system response in a bounded time window within which the interaction takes place, thereby reducing the computational burden. Finally, the aforementioned claims are supported and validated by extensive numerical simulations and tests.

articleTitle: Protection distance for HF communication based on emission standards
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The fast development of new types of energy-smart products has made the regulation of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) falling behind for some areas. Examples of such techniques are solar plants, wireless power transfer for stationary charging of electric vehicles and electric roads. These kinds of installations might generate electromagnetic interference that can interfere with communication systems. To protect the communication system, protection distances around communication receivers need to be introduced.In this work, the necessary protection distance is determined for the high frequency (HF) band 1.6-30 MHz. The potential interference source is assumed to fulfil a certain emission standard limit, such as CISPR 11, EN 50121-2/IEC 62236-2 and IEC 61980. Since HF radios are noise constrained, the protection distance is derived in comparison with the ITU interference category Rural. For the analysis, two different field propagation models for ground wave propagation for HF signals have been evaluated.It is concluded that the investigated ITU model is suitable as a model for the field propagation of the ground wave. The longest protection distance is about 10 km, but the variation is large for different EMC standards, ranging from a couple of hundred meters. The choice of Class A or B levels has a large influence on the protection distance.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of EM Susceptibility of Shielded Objects Based on Susceptibility Pattern
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In this paper a comparative analysis of EM vulnerability of two shielded objects is presented. The analysis is based on the EM susceptibility pattern. The pattern contains information about E-field response to the excitation by uniform plane wave of normalized amplitude and specific polarization within the full solid angle. The susceptibility pattern can be very useful in analysis of EM vulnerability of shielded objects with slots and apertures.

articleTitle: A Macromodeling Approach for EMC Simulations of Power Electronics Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In the past decade, Macromodeling based on the well known Vector Fitting has emerged as the preferred technique to generate passive and causal models from discrete, band limited frequency domain data represented in form of S-parameters. These models can be used in any circuit simulation environment, such as SPICE, for reliable transient and AC analyses. In this paper, we present the application of vector fitting to EMC simulations of power electronics and explain the steps performed during the macromodel generation process in order to help EMC engineers to generate accurate macromodels for switched system simulations.

articleTitle: Harmonic Stability of Grid-connected Voltage Source Converters Considering Parameter Sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of harmonic stabilization based on the parametric sensitivity of voltage source converters (VSCs) operating in parallel. In wind farms and HVDC systems, it needs to take into account the performance of inner current loop or outer voltage loop with the change of the system damping. Uncertainty parameter of controllers can affect the possibility to damp oscillations. This paper proposes a new way using a controlled voltage source to replace VSCs as well as using eigenvalue analysis method for assessing undesirable effects of variable controller parameters on the non-harmonic excitation. Analyzing the simulation results of a representative system in MATLAB/Simulink demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in clarifying harmonic interaction of parallel VSC controllers.

articleTitle: Randomizing Plane-Wave Incidence for Rayleigh Field Synthesis in Reverberation Chambers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Plane-wave (PW) superposition is employed to synthesize accurate electromagnetic field distributions featuring Rayleigh field statistics expected in well-stirred reverberations chambers (RCs). Several angular PW incidence distributions are compared in terms of the field spatial correlation properties. From this comparison it is shown that a spherical spiral sampling scheme provides flexibility to choose an arbitrary number of PW incidence directions while closely approaching the accuracy provided by quasi-optimal Maximum Determinant and Spherical Designs spherical sampling schemes. Finally, it is also shown that random rotations of the constellation of PW incidence direction sets yield much larger RC working volumes compared to a static constellation.

articleTitle: Wide-band Characterization of Multi-Layer Coding Techniques to Achieve Electromagnetic Resilient Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The detection and correction of errors in data transmission over safety-critical communication networks are of utmost importance. Unidentified errors can compromise the system’s functionality in the face of unexpected electromagnetic disturbances. Resilient communication networks are crucial for addressing the aforementioned phenomena. In this paper, a multi-layer coding technique, combining triple modular redundancy and Hamming coding, is proposed to mitigate the impact of EM disturbances over a wide range of frequencies and Signal to Interference Ratio (SIR). The technique’s effectiveness was evaluated through simulations in a reverberating environment, which is an example of a harsh EM environment. The multi-layer technique can reduce the occurrence of undetectable errors from 50% to less than 2%.

articleTitle: Radiofrequency Measuring Receiver with Spectrum Analyzer Function as a Tool for Noise Measurement of Semiconductor Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The article describes the measurement apparatus consisting of a measuring radio frequency receiver working as a spectrum analyzer and specially made amplifiers with very low input noise for the measurement of broadband electrical noise in semiconductor structures and is intentional to measure new structures made of two-dimensional lattices of covalent- and metal-organic frameworks (2D-COF/MOF), belonging to the Dirac family of materials, intended for the construction of the quantum Hall resistance standard (QHRS). The measuring setup operates in the frequency range from 10 kHz to 100 MHz. The implemented variant of the ultra-low noise amplifier (ULNA) improves the noise factor of the receiver five times and allows to obtain of a noise figure value at a level of 0.35 dB. This work proves the usefulness of the EMC receiver in measuring electrical noise using its spectrum analyzer as a modern tool in the search for cross-frequency at the crossover of pink 1/f noise and white noise frequency characteristics if the special construction device like the ULNA is connected at the input of the analyzer.

articleTitle: Reduction of EMC Power Amplifier Intermodulation by Using Digital Signal Predistortion
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The current EMC IEC 61000-4-3 standard includes multiple complex signals like multitone as a possible input signal for radiated immunity test. Nevertheless, due its nonlinear behavior, amplifiers can distort the multitone input signal to some degree, generating intermodulation products at the output which will result in unwanted and additional frequencies applied to the EUT that may affect the results of the test. This paper presents a predistortion method based on the Generalized Memory Polynomial model to compensate for the system nonlinearities. Simulations in MATLAB are performed considering a mathematical model of the physical EMC Sonoma 330 Broadband RF amplifier. The proposed predistortion method could successfully remove the intermodulation distortion products.

articleTitle: Simple Energy-Based Method for Estimating the Equivalent Circuit Parameters of Electrolytic Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: A simple method based on the energy conservation principle is proposed for the estimation of the equivalent circuit parameters of electrolytic capacitors. A series R-L-C circuit model is chosen to describe the real behaviour of these components, which are increasingly used in power converters to realize the DC-bus and filter the generated electromagnetic interference (EMI). The proposed method allows electrolytic capacitors to be characterised in any operating condition and requires only the measurement of the voltage and current waveforms of the capacitor under test.

articleTitle: Impact of Semi-Anechoic Chambers on Magnetic Field Measurements for Frequencies up to 30 MHz
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Over the past years, development of wireless power transfer systems for battery electric vehicles increased noticeably. In order to evaluate these systems regarding their radiated magnetic field emissions in EMC laboratories, it is essential that the measurement results of different test sites are comparable to each other. As absorbers in semi-anechoic chambers are not typically designed for frequencies below 30 MHz, the impact of the test environment onto the measurement results needs to be investigated. In this paper, measurements in the frequency band from 9 kHz to 30 MHz are carried out in a large semi-anechoic chamber suited for test distances of up to 10 m. The measurements are compared to numerical simulation results and a simple simulation model is proposed to estimate the influence of a test site onto measurement results.

articleTitle: A Study on Application of Bulk Current Injection Method as an EMC Test Method for ESD-Induced Conducted Suseptibility on Spacecraft
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In orbiting spacecraft, electrical units may malfunction due to noise caused by electrostatic discharges (ESD) on the spacecraft surface. As a noise propagation model leading to malfunctions, it is known that there is a mode in which electromagnetic noise emitted from the discharge source propagates through free space and irradiates the electrical units.
