There is another mode in which the current resulting from the discharge propagates and flows across the surface of the space structure, is induced in the power and signal harnesses, and enters the electrical unit as conducted noise. Although the ESD generator is a widely used EMC test tool for this noise propagation mode in the spacecraft field, we have been studying to increase the versatility of the test by taking a different approach. This paper presents a study on the application of the bulk current injection method, which is used in the aviation industry for lightning immunity verification, as an immunity test method for ESD-induced conducted currents.

articleTitle: In-Situ and Contactless Evaluation of Performance of Power Converter EMC Filter based on Near-Field Scan Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents and validates an original contactless near-field scan-based method to quantify the performance of EMC filter mounted on power converter boards. The proposed method provides indicators about EMC filter attenuation, decoupling capacitor efficiency and differential-mode to common-mode conversion and may help designer to clarify and debug conducted emission issues of power converter boards.

articleTitle: Effective Inductances of Periodic Perforated Metal Plates for Predicting Microwave Shielding Effectiveness
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents new analytical expressions for the effective inductances of perfectly conductive metal screens that are made up of periodic sub-wavelength circular or square apertures. These expressions are applied to the prediction of the shielding effectiveness (SE) of arrays when excited by oblique incidence plane waves below the cut-off frequency, while taking into account the effect of plate thickness. A new transformation model of two arrays with different hole shapes, assuming the SE as a constraint is proposed. The inductance-based modeling is applied to circular and square pattern configurations in the gigahertz frequency range. The good accuracy of the proposed formulations is demonstrated by comparing the obtained shielding performances with the reference values given by numerical codes or experimental tests. These formulations are easy to use and can provide reliable predictions of the SE of metal screens with periodic sub-wavelength apertures.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Interference Effects from Different Time Domain Signals on WLAN
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: A time domain simulation model to investigate the behavior of different interference signals on WLAN reception is presented. In order to explain the effects of each interference signal a new diagram structure is introduced. A Microwave Oven Leakage signal is applied as interference to characterize its interference behavior. At last a PER simulation method for the prediction of WLAN channel blocking is presented.

articleTitle: Measurement and Simulation of the Shielding Effectiveness of Planar Material with Apertures using a ASTM D4935 TEM Cell
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: To reduce the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions of vehicles during driving and production, a hybrid injection moulding process is being developed for lightweight housings of automotive power electronic modules. During the process, a thin deep-drawn metal sheet is coated with recycled polymer. Back-molded cut-outs are used to form a proper connection between both materials, which is easily recyclable. To ensure the far-field shielding effectiveness (SE), the effect of different apertures in the electromagnetic shield is investigated. This contribution indicates, whether the reduced SE due to apertures can be estimated with a simple transverse electromagnetic (TEM) cell measurement according to the ASTM D4935 standard. This paper presents measurement results of planar metallic material with apertures and with one or two insulating layers. Additionally, a simple simulation model of the TEM cell is presented.

articleTitle: Adjacent channel co-existence study between 5G NR and Wi-Fi in the 6 GHz band for indoor scenario
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This study presents indoor compatibility between Wi-Fi operating in the 5925-6425 MHz band and 5G NR operating in the 6425-7125 MHz band. The study estimates interference levels between 5G NR and Wi-Fi equipment and presents the results as a performance degradation of the 5G NR. The analysis considers two scenarios, the first is a Rician channel between 5G NR and Wi-Fi equipment, and the second is when there is a Rayleigh channel.

articleTitle: An Efficient Neural Network Learning Algorithm for Printed Spiral Coil (PSC) Impedance Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In this paper, a neural network-based learning algorithm is proposed to predict the impedance characteristics of a Printed Spiral Coil (PSC), which is widely used as a structure for Radio-Frequency Interference (RFI) measurement probes. To predict the impedance of PSC, a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) neural network was utilized, and the training data consisted of 604 PSC design structures and self-impedance of PSC corresponding to 600 frequencies. To achieve efficient data learning, a data selection method was proposed using the difference between predicted impedance and target impedance in the high-frequency range. The neural network model with the proposed training data selection algorithm was confirmed to enable efficient learning and accurate impedance prediction with about 16% less training data than the conventional MLP neural network model, and it was validated with accuracy up to 6 GHz through 3D electromagnetic simulation.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Variability of the Maximum Expected Field Strengths in an MRI Room
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe

authors.preferredName: Mark J. A. M. van Helvoort

abstract: This paper defines confidence intervals for the variability of the maximum expected field strengths, at the susceptible frequencies of 1.5T, 3T, and 7T MRI systems. Measurements of the maximum electric field were performed in a 30 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> MRI room. Based on the absolute values of the measurements, an analysis of the undermoded and overmoded properties of the room is presented. Then, the relation between the expected electric field, created by equipment characterized by its TRP, is empirically described. This relation is mainly characterized by the confidence interval of the maximum expected field strength. This confidence interval is a powerful tool to assess the severity of EMC risks.

articleTitle: Comparison of the Damages Produced by Lightning Current Tests for Aircrafts with Unipolar and Oscillatory Waveform for Component A
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Objective of this study is the comparison of the damages produced by unipolar or oscillatory waveform for the lightning current component ‘A’. The component has the peak value of 200 kA and the specific energy of 2•10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> J/Ω. The current parameters represent the lightning threat for aircrafts due to the first return stroke. A variety of specimen were investigated including various metal plates as well as different samples of composite material. All of the specimen exhibited no or no significantly different damages when testing with unipolar or oscillatory current. Obviously, tests with the oscillatory waveform are equivalent to those with unipolar waveform irrespectively of the characteristics of the material.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Electromagnetic Compatibility of Electric City Transport with the Automatics Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper deals with the evaluation on electromagnetic compatibility of city rail transport systems 750 V dc in Ukraine, Indonesia, Malaysia. The results of simulation of electromotive forces at the different frequencies are given. The experimental research of signal current and electromagnetic interferences in the track circuits is shown presence of 300 Hz harmonics near station and 275 Hz on some railway sections, which could be stop movement of trains.

Author Keywords: automatic locomotive signaling system with the automatic regulating speed (ALS-ARS)

articleTitle: Application of Entire Domain Hyper Basis Functions Approach to Solution of EMC Problems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper aims to extend the previously proposed HBF-based MoM approach to analyze EMC problems. This approach uses the eigenfunctions of the generalized eigenvalue equation (GEE) obtained at only one frequency as entire domain hyper basis functions (HBFs) to find the desired solution to the boundary value problem in the broadband frequency range. This paper demonstrates the application of this approach to shielding effectiveness (SE) problems in perforated metallic enclosures, as well as to automotive EMC problems for EMC tests on a car model excited by an impressed current inside the car. The obtained results are verified by comparison with direct MoM results.

articleTitle: Quasi-electrostatic shielding of dissipative cylindrical shells
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe

authors.preferredName: Mark J. A. M. van Helvoort

abstract: A new analytic expression for quasi-electrostatic shielding of a dissipative cylindrical is derived from Maxwell’s equations and validated with simulations. The results clearly demonstrate that a dissipative shield is only effective for preventing the build-up of electrostatic charge. It does not provide full shielding against even slowly varying electric fields.

articleTitle: Improving the performance of characteristic recognition for unknown antennas with limited data
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Identifying the electromagnetic features of an unknown antenna and evaluating its electromagnetic vulnerability are crucial for enhancing the effectiveness of high-power electromagnetic attacks or defenses. Sparse measurement of the radiation pattern combined with Infinitesimal Dipole Modeling (IDM) can be an effective method for antenna modeling. IDM uses mathematical representations of infinitesimal current-carrying elements to model the behavior of the unknown antenna. The more measurement data used, the higher the correlation with the original pattern. However, given the practical limitations of the observation environment, a method of obtaining high correlation with minimal data is necessary. In this paper, a method is presented to probabilistically increase the recognition performance of antenna characteristics, even when IDM is applied with limited data. This is achieved by utilizing general electromagnetic properties of antennas and data augmentation. A simulation and measurement were conducted using a rigid horn antenna. The results showed that the same correlation performance can be achieved with IDM enhanced by data augmentation, compared to traditional IDM, even when using fewer measurement points.

articleTitle: Shielded Aircraft Windows to Protect Radio Altimeters in the Presence of Wireless Avionics Intra-Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Wireless Avionics Intra-Communications in the frequency range of 4.2 to 4.4 GHz is an upcoming solution to replace the cabling of part of the data network in aircraft with a wireless alternative. This solution shares its frequency band with the radio altimeter and is therefore subject to limitations on the transmitted power to ensure compatibility with flight critical equipment of the aircraft. This paper presents simulation results on the effectiveness of shielded aircraft windows to protect radio altimeters in the presence of wireless avionics intra-communication. A propagation model is developed to simulate how shielded cabin windows affect the EIRP of WAIC transmitters within the cabin of an aircraft. Simulation with this model show that a reduction in EIRP of roughly 15 dB can be expected when electromagnetic coating is applied to the passenger windows. These results can be used in the design of robust WAIC network solutions that are compatible with legacy aircraft equipment.

articleTitle: Estimating the Optimal Polynomial Order for the Vector Fitting Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper offers a method to find the optimal polynomial order for the Vector Fitting algorithm. An exemplary artificial transfer function was used to investigate the fundamental bias-variance trade-off of the vector fitting model. By solving a bounded optimization problem and using the method of the golden-section search, the optimal polynomial order for the vector fitting algorithm can be found in an computationally efficient way. The performance and limitations of the proposed method are evaluated against different signal-to-noise ratios. Preliminary experimental results demonstrate the need and strength of the method.

articleTitle: Analysis of aircraft shieldings for lightning indirect effects by a novel S-FDTD
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents an extension of the stochastic FDTD method to predict the variance of fields coupled through multilayered lossy thin panels. The subgridding boundary condition subcell model is employed in an unconditional Crank-Nicolson formulation. A discussion on the effect of the influence of material parameters is done in the context of the assessment of the shielding effectiveness of typical aircraft fuselages.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Impact of Differential Transfer Efficiency of EM Leakage on Screen Reconstruction against High-Resolution Displays
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In TEMPEST attacks targeting high-resolution displays that divide the screen into multiple areas, the reconstruction of screen information is difficult owing to multiple emanation sources. This is because each pixel is transmitted on a different path, which causes overlap of pixel information on reconstructed images. To solve this, we have proposed a reconstruction method of images on display with multiple areas based on the differences in transfer efficiencies between emanation sources on each screen area and the measurement point and consequently separating each screen information. However, we confirmed that variation in reconstruction accuracies of information is dependent on measurement parameters used to cause differences in transfer efficiencies. The selection of measurement parameters that renders highly accurate reconstruction has yet to be investigated. In this study, we investigated the effects of measurement parameters on the reconstruction accuracy of a reconstructed image, focusing on measurement positions and receiving frequencies as measurement parameters to vary transfer efficiencies. Specifically, the evaluation of the effects of measurement positions and receiving frequencies on transfer efficiencies was rendered possible by controlling radiation intensity based on operations of the screen image and measuring their spectrum. In addition, the reconstruction accuracy of reconstructed images was evaluated while altering measurement parameters using convolutional neural networks. The above evaluations indicate that the reconstruction rate was approximately 38% in cases involving the alteration of measurement positions, whereas it was approximately 62% in cases altering receiving frequencies. Therefore, it was confirmed that the alteration of receiving frequencies can improve the separation accuracy of screen information, resulting in high information reconstruction rate.

articleTitle: Modulation Frequency Effects on the Spread-Spectrum Clocking
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Spread-spectrum technique is employed in Buck converters to minimize electromagnetic emissions. This is achieved by distributing the electromagnetic interference around the switching frequency in a frequency band, which leads to a reduction in the amplitude of the interference. This peak reduction depends on the modulation frequency and the bandwidth of the applied spread-spectrum technique. This paper presents a spread-spectrum controller with a controllable modulation frequency which generates pseudo-random clock signal. The controller is used to investigate the effects of the modulation frequency on the frequency spectrum of the generated clock signal. The measurements show that the peak reduction is proportional to the modulation frequency in the case of the quasi-peak detector, while the peak reduction is inversely proportional to the modulation frequency in the case of the average detector. The measurements also show that the pseudo-random clock signal generated by the long period linear shift register has a more even frequency spectrum.

articleTitle: Effect of Environment of Dual Vibrating Intrinsic Reverberation Chamber on Dynamic Range for Shielding Effectiveness Measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents the effect of a reflective environment of the dual vibrating intrinsic reverberation chamber (dual VIRC) on the dynamic range (DR) for shielding effectiveness (SE) measurements. The DR of the same dual VIRC setup is shown for different reflective environments. The effect of leakage of the cloth material of the dual VIRC on the DR in such a reflective environment has been investigated too.

Author Keywords: dual vibrating intrinsic reverberation chamber (dual VIRC)

articleTitle: Validation procedures for EMC Test Sites in the frequency range 1 to 18 GHz in view of extension to the frequency range 18 to 40 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper shows a comparison of two methods for the Site VSWR measurement for anechoic room validation. The CISPR method based on CISPR 16-1-4 is compared with the ANSI C63.25.1 method. Differences will be analyzed and necessary technical concretizations in the standard are explained. This is important to provide a technically solid base for the anechoic room validation for continuously increasing frequencies above 18 GHz.

articleTitle: Utilization of the Return Conductor for Cancellation of CM Currents for a PMSM Inverter Drive
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper describes an injection method for the reduction of Common Mode (CM) noise. This is done for a drive train of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine (PMSM) with an inverter where there is a pre-defined return path for All Electric Aircraft (AEA). A simplified model is presented which shows the potential of this type of injection, by which it is expanded to a three-phase system by use of a PMSM model. In the lower frequency range, below 1 MHz, the Insertion Loss (IL) is still at a constant level. This can lead to further reduction of the volume and weight of the Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) filter by shifting the cutoff frequency of the passive filter.

articleTitle: FDTD Full Wave Simulations of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents the analysis of metasurfaces, here called reconfigurable intelligent surface. The analysis is performed by numerical simulations that implement the finite-difference time-domain method. The metasurface has been mod-eled by metallic patches interconnected by varactor diodes. The electromagnetic source consists of randomly generated plane wave. This kind of analysis allows us to investigate the response of the metasurface when it is hit by a random source.

articleTitle: EMC Study of Automotive Wire Harness Configurations in a GTEM Cell
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In a modern vehicle, the automotive wire harness forms a crucial part of the sensor signal and power distribution system. It is thus important to understand the impact of electromagnetic interference on such harness, in particular its dependence on layout with respect to an incoming electromagnetic wave. The research presented here investigates the induced common-mode and differential-mode currents in various wire harness layouts, as well as the dependence on both grounding and on the harness design involving an unshielded twisted or untwisted pair. The results indicate that for harness layouts with a substantial component along the electric field directions, such current levels can reach up to those that disrupt automotive sensor communication.

articleTitle: Improvement in Low Frequency Emission Test Method by Live Impedance Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The MIL-STD-461 CE101 test is one of the essential low frequency emission tests in the range of 30 Hz – 10 kHz for military and aerospace equipment, however, its application remains challenging. The primary concern is the effect of the power source or grid impedance on test results because the LISNs are not functional in such a low frequency range. Therefore, the emission levels depend on the source impedance and, consequently, the reproducibility of test results is generally poor. In this paper, we thoroughly analyse this problem and propose a solution based on the live impedance measurement of the CE101 test circuit. For the live impedance measurement, we used the CS101 military low frequency immunity test system along with the addition of FFT and current measurement capabilities.

articleTitle: Discussion of the height scan introduced in CISPR 32 for measuring emissions above 1 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper discusses the introduction of the antenna height scan in CISPR 32 Ed. 2.1 from technical and economical point of view. An artificial equipment under test (EUT) has been examined in an absorber-lined semi-anechoic chamber and a fully anechoic room. The influence of insufficient floor absorber layout and antenna tilting on the height scan is presented by measurements and calculations. The paper closes with a description of the relation between the measurement method, the measurand and the definition of limits with respect to the disturbance scenario (CISPR 16-4-4) and the challenges of EMC measurements with modern electric systems.

articleTitle: Short pulse testing of a reference test setup in a reverberation chamber of two different time constants
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The increasing threat from high power electromagnetic weapons necessitates further research in pulsed high level testing in order to accurately assess the potential damage it can cause. This study is part of an ongoing collaboration where a reference test setup has previously been developed to facilitate exchange of test results between different laboratories. The purpose is to examine results from pulsed tests that have been conducted in reverberation chamber with different time constants for pulse widths of 600 ns. We find that there is some discrepancy between the two chamber configurations when different predefined errors of the test setup occur. Finally, the pulse waveforms at the receiving antenna in the chamber are measured.

articleTitle: FPGA Based Motor Inverter Control for Strictly Synchronous Digital Active EMI Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Many modern motor inverters use fast switching transistors to reduce losses. Due to steep switching waveforms and high frequencies, these systems represent a significant source of electromagnetic interference (EMI). Usually, large and heavy passive filters are used to suppress the EMI. Active EMI filters (AEF) can reduce the size and weight. Digital AEFs with synthesized anti-noise injection can reach very high performance when the injected anti-noise is synchronized to the EMI that has to be measured in advance. Unavoidable delays between EMI measurement and anti-noise injection lead to reduced suppression at higher frequencies. A prediction of future EMI allows compensation of delays and thus synchronous injection. In motor inverters, the control signals contain important EMI information for predicting the needed anti-noise signal. As the control signal is created first, knowledge on it can give sufficient advance for anti-noise processing. Furthermore, for a high noise suppression a strict temporal relation between EMI and anti-noise is needed. This can be achieved, e.g., if motor control and anti-noise signal generation are implemented with a common clock or on a single signal processing system. As several investigations have shown that a field-programmable gate arrays (FPGA) combined with fast digital-to-analog and analog-to-digital converters are appropriate for anti-noise signal generation, it is obvious to also implement the noise generation algorithm on the same FPGA. In this work first, a synchronous motor control and digital AEF system are discussed. Especially, a digital adaptive notch filter has been developed that is operated synchronously with the noise source. The performance of this filter is discussed.

articleTitle: Physics-based and Behavioural Models for the Dynamic Response of a TVS Diode
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Prediction of the dynamic response of ESD protections is necessary for system-efficient ESD design (SEED). This paper proposes two models reproducing the features of the dynamic response of a transient-voltage suppressor (TVS) diode subjected to transmission-line pulses (TLP). A physical model including bipolar operation, avalanche and conductivity modulation along with the various delays associated with the build-up of charges in the structure is shown to capture all key features of the dynamic response. A behavioural model, focussed on the activation process and conductivity modulation achieves comparable results.

articleTitle: Contribution from 4G/5G networks into the electromagnetic environment in the railway stations in Warszawa
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The aim of this study was to evaluate parameters of electromagnetic radiation (EMR) exposure caused by radiocommunication systems in urban environment on the example of the 3 railway stations in Warszawa. The exposure were analysed with the use of frequency-selective data loggers of RMS value of electric field strength covering selected frequency bands of its dominating components (RTV transmitters, GSM 900 DL, merged LTE (800, 800, 2100 and 2600 DL) used by 4G and emerging 5G standards of radiocommunication) and for broadband RMS value of all components. Higher levels of exposure on the platforms located on the ground in comparison to underground ones was found (medians/95<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> percentile values: 0.12/0.21 V/m in RTV bands, 0.24/0.42 V/m in GSM 900 band, 0.50/0.89 V/m in LTE bands and 0.58/0.95 V/m for broadband results on the ground platforms, and respectively: 0.04/0.06 V/m; 0.08/0.38 V/m; 0.10/0.43 and 0.17/0.55 V/m on the underground platforms). Also higher levels of exposure were found in 2022 compared to 2021 because of increased traffic of travellers – in the main halls (medians/95th percentile values were: 0.24/0.65 V/m in LTE bands and 0.37/0.96 V/m for broadband results in 2022, and respectively: 0.16/0.43 V/m and 0.26/0.65 V/m for this bands in 2021).

articleTitle: Reducing Parasitic Capacitances of Ring-Core Inductors
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In this work, we analyze the impact of the permittivity of the material of the core and of the configuration of the winding on the parasitic capacitance that typically undermines the performance of ring-core inductors at high frequencies. Inductors with NiZn and MnZn ferrite cores and with both loose and tight windings have been constructed, measured and compared. Also, a high-frequency circuit model of the inductors has been employed along with a simple characterization technique to obtain equivalent circuits of the ring-core inductors. This has allowed us to quantify the impact of the different core choices and winding strategies on the performance of the inductors up to frequencies of at least 30 MHz. Our results demonstrate that the parasitic capacitance of single-layer ring core inductors can be reduced by using winding strategies that are different for NiZn and MnZn cores. We conclude that the different responses of inductors made with different core materials is due to the differences in the permittivity of the ferrite materials of the core.

articleTitle: A Multivariate Approach for the Effective Sample Size of Frequency Stirring
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: We introduce a new method for the estimation of the effective sample size due to frequency stirring in reverberation chambers. The method is based on a multivariate approach, which is able to estimate the single-level correlation of frequency stirring, based on two-, or many-levels correlations due to concurrent stirring mechanisms. We confront the estimations of the effective sample size due to frequency stirring from our method with theoretical predictions. The comparison with theory, shown here for the first time, allows for a deeper confidence on the validity of our proposed method. The agreement is shown for different types of reverberation chambers, at different loading conditions for wide frequency ranges.

articleTitle: Machine-Learning-Based Parameterization of Adaptive Notch Filters for CM Noise Reduction in Motor Inverters
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Fast-switching semiconductor components are increasingly used in motor inverters for drive systems. The short rise times and high voltage levels improve the efficiency of the devices but lead to an increase in electromagnetic emissions. The conducted emissions are typically reduced with filters. Active EMI filters (AEF) promise weight and volume reduction compared to passive filters. Digital AEF (DAEF) concepts offer noise suppression at higher frequencies, but adjustment of a large number of filter parameters can be challenging. The dependence of the many parameters on each other and the strong non-linearity of the DAEF often lead to unexpected behavior. In this paper, a parameter optimization algorithm based on supervised learning is proposed for the design of a special kind of DAEF. The aim is to find the optimal parameters for several adaptive notch DAEFs to reduce EMI noise in a wide frequency range. The new approach is implemented and tested for applicability in a simplified laboratory setup.

Author Keywords: narrow band adapted digital active EMI filter (NADAEF)

articleTitle: PEEC-based Wideband Micro-Model of Inductive Components for Power Electronics Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents modeling approach for the fast and accurate simulations of the power inductors with toroidal core. The proposed method is developed in order to generate a wideband micro-model of a common-mode (CM) chokes represented as Partial Element Equivalent Circuit (PEEC). The combination of the analytical solution and 2D static simulation is used to obtain the values of the physical parameters for PEEC, such as the self and mutual inductances and capacitances. The circuit simulations of the PEEC-based model of choke gives possibility to calculate accurately the CM and DM impedances or S-parameters and analyze behavior of the choke over a wide frequency range (from DC up to 100MHz). The validation of the PEEC-based micro-model is done for the chokes with different complexity of the windings using experimental data. Finally, application of the developed modeling technique is demonstrated for EMC filter with different CM choke samples. Impact of the power inductor performance on the filter’s attenuation is analyzed.

articleTitle: Dynamic Propagation Channel Evaluation with Software Defined Radio Architectures
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This contribution discusses a software defined radio (SDR) measurement environment for emulating dynamic propagation channels and a corresponding analysis of the receiver settings’ effects. As a fundamental example to be investigated, a scenario with a moving aircraft in landing approach is taken with a commercially available navigation receiver, the settings of which can be adjusted. The corresponding synthesis of the navigation signal to be fed into the SDR is explained. It comprises both the conversion from the navigation signal of an antenna array in spatial domain to the time domain and the sampling of the aircraft’s motion. Measurements with a navigation receiver validate the SDR environment, and finally a dynamic multipath propagation scenario is set up to demonstrate the effect of the receiver’s setting, such as measurement time. With respect to electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) the proposed SDR environment allows an application-based assessment of error contributions, e.g., due to multipath propagation, which exceeds the usual EMC concept of solely static limits for system disturbances. Additionally, hardware requirements of the SDR are addressed.

articleTitle: "Fifty Shades of Grey and More": Medical Use of Systems of Systems, Trends, Challenges and, Implications for EMC
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The complexity and diversity of medical electrical equipment and their intended use environments are increasing. The complexity and diversity make clinical environments "grey" in terms of EM behaviour compared to controlled laboratory environments in which they are tested for EMC compliance. Different clinical environments (even functionally similar ones) may have different EM behaviour making them have different "shades of grey" compared to each other depending on factors such as types of equipment, the density of equipment, and structural differences. On the other hand, the susceptibility of medical devices to EMI (Electromagnetic Interference) tends to increase posing more challenges [1]. This "greyness" due to the growing complexity of medical equipment and their intended use environments and increasing susceptibility has led to unprecedented EMC concerns. This paper briefs current trends in the clinical use of systems of systems (SoS), challenges that arise regarding EMC/EMI and suggestions for potential ways to address such challenges in the medical technology domain.

articleTitle: Predictive sensitivity analysis of motor’s windings HF impedances
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper describes a process in which high frequency (HF) differential-mode (DM) and common-mode (CM) impedances of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) are predicted. These tools, using both 2D Finite Element Modeling (FEM) and Spice lumped parameter circuit, are then used to generate sensibilities analysis such as Sobol and Correlation indices with the help of surrogate models. This method gives a better understanding of design choices that can be made to impact impedances values at both low and high frequency for a same load working point. Obtained simulation results are compared to experimental ones using statistics, showing the interest of such an approach.

articleTitle: Risk of EMI due to Necessary Modification in a Remote Microgrid in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: There are many challenges in maintaining the sustainability of microgrids in remote areas, one of them being early failures of the components. Due to limited access and resources, solutions that are quick, cheap, and easily obtainable are used to fix the failed components. Therefore, systems with ad-hoc modifications are typically found, which are deemed necessary for the system operation. Through on-site voltage and current measurements, this paper investigates the additional risk of failure due to electromagnetic interference (EMI) that is introduced by necessary ad-hoc modifications in a remote microgrid in Indonesia. There are two separate microgrids (microgrid 1 and 2) with a desalination system connected to microgrid 1. Failures were found, which required the desalination system to be connected to microgrid 2. The results show that the modification in microgrid 2 reduced the efficiency of the battery inverter, increased voltage harmonics, and made the microgrid more susceptible to an inrush current. The findings corroborate the importance of remote EMI measurements and monitoring to get insight into potential risks and undertake timely measures. This is crucial, especially in remote areas where repair and replacement could be costly.

articleTitle: Hints and ideas on customising the EMC engineering approach for CubeSat projects
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) is a critical discipline in ensuring the reliable functioning of CubeSats. However, CubeSats are typically very small satellites that have limited space packed with various electronic systems. The unique features of CubeSat projects - such as their small scale, short development cycles, and a higher tolerance for mission failure risks - asks for a customised EMC engineering approach that strikes a project-specific balance between maintaining an essential reliability and the benefits of the low-cost and fast development cycle. In this paper, some hints and ideas for customising EMC engineering for CubeSat projects are presented. It is focused on a selection of essential parts, e.g., basic EMC requirements, analysis, designing and testing.

articleTitle: Characterization of High Voltage EMC filters for Electric Vehicles charging applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Filters for Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) are necessary since they can suppress the noise coming from switching-mode power supplies (SMPS). A key component of such filters are common mode chokes (CMCs) and film filter capacitors. In Electric Vehicles (EVs) charging applications such as On-Board Chargers (OBCs), the power EMC filters are located at the input side, the AC High Voltage (HV) filter and output side DC HV filter. In particular, the second one is the device that interfaces the charger with the Li-ion HV vehicle battery. CISPR25 regulates the EMI noise level on the HV port, however car-makers can have their own EMC regulations with more challenging limits with respect to the international norm. Prediction of the performances of the filter is necessary to avoid time-consuming hit-and-trial set of measurements in anechoic chambers to find root cause of filter failure. This paper deals with the simulation performed with Ansys HFSS and characterization of an HV DC filter for a 22kW/800V OBC mounted on a high-end car. Emphasis is put on dealing with chassis enclosure, necessary to shield filter as well for cooling purposes, which might alter filter performances.

articleTitle: Power Line Communications for Avionics Systems: Robustness Against Electromagnetic Compatibility
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Electrification of numerous aircraft systems over the course of the past decades has caused a significant increase in weight and complexity of onboard power and data networks, and this trend is expected to continue on the road towards sustainable aviation. Hybrid data networks that combine conventional cabling with wireless technologies and power line communication have the potential to yield data networks with reduced weight. However, in doing so, safety should not be compromised. Therefore, this paper presents the results of a measurement campaign that was carried out to investigate the robustness of Power Line Communications with respect to Electromagnetic Compatibility. The tests include conducted susceptibility, as well as conducted and radiated emissions. Three different wiring configurations were tested, being a single wire and bifilar wire with structure as return, complemented by a wire pair with dedicated return wire. Overall, except for the single wire case, Power Line Communications performed well on all tests, with the bifilar wiring case slightly outperforming the wire pair case. Resonance phenomena observed in conducted emission results are explained by additional simulations.

articleTitle: Intersystem-Interference Consequences in Ultra-Dense Scenarios for 6G
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The development of mobile technologies is going on for the future 6G concept. 6G is aiming towards considerably higher frequencies and ultra-dense co-location scenarios of electronic equipment. From an Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) point of view it is important to analyze the interference consequences in such scenarios. In this paper, an analysis of EMC consequences in such ultra-dense scenarios is performed. The analysis is done for both unintentional and intentional radiated emission from transmitting equipment. It is shown how the compatibility margin between radiated emission limits and radiated susceptibility limits is considerably decreased in these scenarios. Furthermore, it is shown how the ultra-dense scenarios give an accumulated interference level in the communication receivers at the higher frequencies predicted for 6G.

articleTitle: Smart Input Space Sampling Combined with Kriging-Partial Least Square Regression for EMC Risk Analysis at PCB Level with Many Variables
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This article describes an advanced methodology for training surrogate models (SMs) in order to study the sensitivity of many geometrical parameters of printed circuit boards (PCBs) for a quicker investigation of routing rules regarding potential electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) or signal integrity (SI) issues. This methodology consists in two steps. First, it retains only the sensitive parameters of the input space that mostly explain the several output observations. Second, it consists in training iteratively several competing SMs, selecting the most efficient one, regarding training time and/or accuracy. Here, the Kriging-partial least square Regression (K-PLS) is identified as a relevant method for the considered case study, which consists of a 17-parameter multiple outputs crosstalk scenario. An extreme value analysis is provided as an outcome for a possible adjustment of design rules.

articleTitle: Effects of Feedback Report with Objectively Measured Radio-Frequency Electromagnetic Fields (RF-EMF) Levels on Recipient’s Subjective RF-EMF Exposure Levels
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In this study, we focused on the feedback report of objectively measured radio-frequency electromagnetic field (RF-EMF) levels obtained by in-home and microenvironmental exposure monitoring and assessed its impact on the recipient’s awareness of RF-EMF and subjective RF-EMF exposure levels. Factors such as knowledge level, risk perception, and the objectively measured RF-EMF levels presented in the feedback report were also examined as possible factors affecting the results. Twenty-nine valid answers collected by questionnaire surveys at two-time points (pre- and post-feedback) were analyzed. Results showed that the level of awareness of RF-EMF altered after becoming aware of the feedback report, and the understandability of the feedback report was a possible factor affecting the results. Higher needs for RF-EMF-utilizing activities and knowledge of high exposure levels (≥ median) resulted in higher awareness. Furthermore, the provision of information helped to envision subjective RF-EMF exposure levels and led to a decrease in answering "no idea" regarding subjective RF-EMF levels. Factors possibly affecting the subjective RF-EMF levels were gender, fear of health effects, subjective knowledge, and risk perception of RF-EMF prior to feedback. Subjective RF-EMF exposure levels were significantly lower in respondents who received results of higher exposure levels (≥ median). These results are providing insights regarding the association of information provision and respondent’s subjective RF-EMF exposure levels and would be useful for developing adequate risk communication strategies for the general public and workers at risk of high exposure.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic shielding properties of impact damaged carbon and hybrid carbon and glass fibre reinforced polymer composites
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Although the investigation of electromagnetic shielding properties of carbon fibre reinforced composites has increased over the last years, the topic of electromagnetic shielding durability received relatively little attention. The aim of this study was to systematically examine the effect of low velocity impact damage on the shielding effectiveness (SE) of continuous carbon and hybrid carbon/glass fibre reinforced polymer composites with various lay-ups. The SE measurements were carried out in a high frequency range (26-42 GHz) using free-space method with focusing lenses. It was observed that when the carbon fibre splitting occurred on the bottom carbon fibre ply oriented parallel to the incident electric field, the SE was noticeably reduced. Adding glass fibre plies with higher, compared to carbon fibres, strain-to-failure improved the impact resistance and thus delayed the threshold for SE reduction. Overall, it is demonstrated that, due to the synergistic effects, properly designed hybrid carbon/glass fibre composites can be used for lightweight electromagnetic shielding structures, whose shielding properties are maintained even after sustaining a mechanical damage.

articleTitle: Python-LTSpice Framework for Multi-Objective EMC Filter Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: EMC filters should ensure that a device complies with respective regulations, but at the same time should be as small and cheap as possible. Besides the compliance with EMI limits, all used filter components also need to withstand the rated current and voltage of the specific application. For real products this constitutes a discrete valued optimization task, as components and especially common-mode chokes (CMC) are usually not available in all sizes. This work proposes the application of a sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-II) for described optimization problem. The presented workflow builds on freely available tools, namely LTSpice for circuit simulation and the Python libraries PyLTSpice and pymoo. For demonstration, a commercially available EMC filter design kit is used. From 696 possible component combinations the optimal common-mode (CM) filter for a frequency range of 9 kHz - 100 MHz is found, considering price, volume, ampacity and PCB parasitics.

articleTitle: Measurement and Simulation Methodology for Characterizing the Shielding Effectiveness of Coating Materials for Optical Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Effective shielding of radiated emissions of ICs is of vital importance in today’s densely packed mobile devices. Since space is very limited in most applications, the mounting of large shielding caps with appropriate grounding is not an efficient solution. This paper investigates the shielding efficiency of space-saving coating materials for optical sensor lids with apertures. The shielding efficiency of coating materials is evaluated for functional sensor devices as well as for simple test structures by means of measurements according to the respective standard. The simple test structures are also used to investigate the influence of the grounding path of the shield. It is shown that solid grounding is crucial for effective RF shielding. Furthermore, a simulation strategy is presented which allows the prediction of the shielding effectiveness of coated sensor lids by means of full wave finite element simulations.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Susceptibility of a Connected System Against Intentional Electromagnetic Interferences Assessment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The Internet of Things is a concept that allows the interoperability of embedded systems through an Internet connection. It is increasingly used in fields such as: healthcare, transport and home automation industries. The systems designed for the Internet of Things are more and more used in applications with a high-level of operational safety. Therefore, their reliability has to be ensured in particular in the harsh environment in which they operate. In this study, a connected system has been developed and exposed to Intentional Electromagnetic Interferences to assess its susceptibility. The electromagnetic disturbances are transmitted to the system through two injection methods: the GTEM cell and the Near Field injection methods. The induced failures of the device under test have been characterized according to the injected signal parameters such as its frequency and its power.

articleTitle: Prediction Accuracy Improvement of Side-channel Information Leakage by Using EM-Circuit Co-simulation of PDN with Filters
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Ever since the side-channel attack (SCA) was proposed, there is a danger that the secret key used for encryption can be recovered by analyzing the noise in the power supply system. Therefore, it is important to predict the extent to which electromagnetic interference (EMI) measures can suppress such attack. To predict power noise and SCA, models of IC and a power distribution network (PDN) are required. Previous studies have targeted the case of implementing one decoupling capacitor on the PDN to evaluate the validity of the IC model, as well as the application of an equivalent circuit model of the PDN. In the current work, to improve the prediction accuracy when multiple decoupling capacitors are mounted, we examined the application of an electromagnetic (EM) field and circuit co-simulation. In this co-simulation, ports are placed at the mounting points of the electronic components on the EM field model of PDN. We then obtain a PDN multi-port network, and connect it to the electronic components in a circuit simulator. Finally, the transfer impedance from the IC to the measurement port is predicted by circuit simulation. This improves the prediction accuracy because the couplings between components are included in the analysis. In addition, multiple decoupling conditions can be evaluated at high speed because the capacitor mounting conditions on the circuit model can be changed. We implemented an AES circuit on the FPGA and predicted power noise and SCA. The results show that the prediction accuracy of noise and SCA is improved.

articleTitle: Performance Charaterisation of the Decoupling Capacitor Network using the Near-Field Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper describes a contactless method for evaluating the performance of a decoupling capacitor network and diagnose power integrity issues. A performance indicator is extracted for each capacitor from the near-field measurements (based on Z21 impedance measurement). Quantitative performance indicators extracted can provide in-depth analysis of the effect of the design of power network. The influence of each capacitor on the overall network impedance can be clearly identified and the impact of other contributors in the power network (PCB, IC and regulator) can also be analyzed. Using the near-field measurement allows to have a relevant approach (contactless, accurate and very wide band) to analyze decoupling capacitance network.

articleTitle: On the Measurement of Far Field Intensities Generated by Cables Shielded With Composites Showing Electromagnetic Losses
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Electromagnetic compatibility is a significant problem for electronic system developers, especially cabling, which is often the weakest link of the assembly, therefore a bigger emphasis is put on its securing. Recently, a significant progress has been achieved in synthetic electromagnetically lossy materials. Therefore, new cable designs using these cable sheath materials can be soon expected both in applied research and in development. At the same time, reliable measurements of such shielding effectiveness are needed, especially in terms of the far field. While most publications about synthetic electromagnetic lossy materials deal with their measurement via coaxial transmission lines (the ASTM method), far-field measurements have not been sufficiently discussed. In this paper, several phenomena related to this topic are discussed, further, an experiment testing two different cable specimens is realized and the results are compared. The paper discusses fundamental issues of far EM field generated by power supply cables fed by radio frequency interferences.

articleTitle: Simulation of Resonances in Power Electronic Circuits for EMC Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The use of wide-bandgap semiconductors in modern power electronics creates new challenges in EMC. These result, among other things, from high frequencies and steep switching slopes. In addition, parasitic elements of semiconductors, passive components and the printed circuit board can cause resonances, which become noticeable in oscillations. In this work, a possibility is presented to simulate resonances in a power electronic circuit. The circuit used is a series-LC resonant converter with SiC-MOSFETs. An impedance model of the resonant load is generated with consideration of parasitic elements. The accurate simulation is validated by comparison with time domain measurements. EMC measurements of conducted and radiated emissions are done. It is shown that the resonances lead to emissions which can be predicted using the time domain simulation.

articleTitle: Susceptible Frequency Range Definition for Robust Immunity Tests
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Systems containing lithium-ion batteries are shown to require a longer dwell time to properly perform an immunity test due to their vulnerability to thermal runaway effects. Since thermal processes generally take longer than the standards require for testing, the need for longer dwell time can easily be overlooked. This paper highlights the procedure to estimate the narrow frequency band in which such equipment is the most vulnerable to disturbances, and where longer dwell time should be used. This paper discusses different approaches for determining such a frequency range. In particular, the approach utilizing input impedance measurements is examined in the case of a device containing a lithium-ion battery. The analysis is performed on a simulated circuit as well as based on measurements of an assembled unit representing complex equipment under test.

articleTitle: A study on the characteristics of signal transmission in the electronic brake system for autonomous driving
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In electric vehicles for the autonomous driving, most driving systems require redundant designs to overcome significant functional problems. However, added design causes a problem of arranging parts in the vehicle and increase in the cost of the product. Therefore, the electronic brake system including a redundant design in the form of one box is being developed to solve the space and cost problem. This electronic brake system have mechanical parts that are shared by two separate electric systems, thereby minimizing the increase in the size of parts and the increase in the cost of parts. And for the communication between separated systems in one package, the metal structures are being used to connect two system. The signal integrity between the two systems that are connected by metal structure is very weak because of the discontinuous signal line. Also, there is a problem of signal distortion due to the coupling caused by high current system such as motor inverter circuit in the electronic brake system. In this paper, a design for improving the signal transmission performance between two systems is proposed through 3D EM simulation and verified through actual measurement.

articleTitle: Educational Demo’s for Showing the Influence of (im)proper Installation and Grounding of Filters
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The need of implementing low-pass filters to protect sensitive equipment from high-frequency noise, and reverse, increases as technology develops. However, for efficient filter operation, it is important to ensure its proper installation, with a focus on ensuring a secure and stable ground connection. This paper presents setups for educational purposes as part of electrical engineering courses, in order to demonstrate how the performance of a passive filter depends on the quality of its grounding. The designed units are used to measure the filter's insertion loss in various modes: normal mode, differential mode and common mode. Analytical methods describing the operation of the filter and simulation of its performance using LTSpice XVII have been performed to explain the processes more clearly, and to explain the concept of impedance mismatch and modes for filters.

articleTitle: Lessons from Proficiency Testing in EMC
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Since 2016, METAS organized numerous proficiency testing schemes for EMC laboratories. This experience demonstrated the benefit of the proficiency testing. This publication aims to provide some examples of the problems, or of the inappropriate application of the EMC testing, that were observed during the interlaboratory comparison campaigns. It can be emphasised that these findings have always been discussed with the participants and that it led to an improvement of their test setups and procedures. These examples might also be beneficial to the whole EMC community.

articleTitle: Deploying a Continuous Wave Electromagnetic Disturbance Removal Algorithm on an OFDM System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper describes the physical validation of the continuous wave electromagnetic disturbance removal algorithm for orthogonal frequency division multiplexing communication systems. The validation is done by deploying the algorithm in a laboratory setting. Due to the assumptions being made during the simulation process of the algorithm, the validation process describes the key aspects that must be taken into account during actual deployment. For instance, it is shown that in orthogonal frequency division multiplexing-based systems, a continuous wave disturbance can completely break equalization. Therefore, to perform validation, the disturbance has to be injected so that it will not affect the signal’s preamble. During the validation, it was shown that the algorithm under investigation is effective and can result in the algorithm’s gain of more than 18 dB for specific bit error rate ratios and modulation schemes.

articleTitle: Challenges in Risk-based EMC for MRI Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe

authors.preferredName: Mark J. A. M. van Helvoort

abstract: This paper gives an overview of risk-based EMC for high-field strength magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) systems. The challenges when applying this approach are described. First, the unreliability of on-site testing inside hospitals unveils the need to correlate in-situ measurements with measurements performed in an EMC laboratory. For MRI systems, this is particularly challenging due to the undermoded behavior of its electromagnetic environment. Second, state-of-the-art risk analysis techniques oversimplify the complexity of novel and innovative medical equipment. To deal with this complexity, new approaches to risk analysis are required. A promising technique is STPA, which not only considers risk due to component failures, but also due to complex interactions between hardware, software, and human components.

articleTitle: Detection and Localization of CDM like ESD using a novel Sensor derived from Leaky-Coax
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Downscaled semiconductors are at risk of CDM like ESD events during manufacturing, packaging, testing and placement. The reduction in silicon area spent for ESD protection circuits in modern ICs makes the devices more vulnerable by reducing damaging thresholds. Following this trend in industry it is getting more crucial to monitor ESD in processes where these devices are handled. A new type of sensor using multiple antennas along a coax-cable is used to locate CDM like ESD events. Due to the large quantity of antennas, this sensor has the potential to be used in more complex environments where a line of sight is not necessary for all antennas. The localization is performed based on an algorithm which compares the measured signal with a reference dataset from simulation. A hardware implementation together with a stepwise derivation of the algorithm is described. Evaluation of the system in an initial setup is showing encouraging performance for the localization.

articleTitle: The nature of radiofrequency electromagnetic exposure to outdoor workers active in the harbour versus the city centre
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Harbours (HBs) are the open areas of specific environmental properties comparing to nearby city centres (CCs). The open space of HBs and boats (open decks) need to be managed by outdoor workers who are assisting passengers and freight, cleaning, removing the snow, etc. Such outdoor personnel is a subject of electromagnetic radiation (EMR) exposure caused by various radio communications fixed emitters, located inside, near or far from HB. This paper is discussing the results of pilot studies on the nature of radiofrequency EMR exposures to the outdoor workers - to compare whether the frequency pattern of EMR exposure differs between the outdoor environment of civil HBs and CCs, to define the relevant measurement procedure and devices to cover sufficiently all significant frequency contributions of total EMR exposure within further steps of planned studies. By the use of the frequency-selective measurements by portable, autonomous, radiofrequency exposure data-loggers, it was found the significantly different relative contribution of EMR exposure caused by emissions from the radio-television (RTV) broadcasting emitters and stationary antennas of public mobile communication systems for voice (GSM) and data (LTE) communications – GSM-LTE emissions are dominating in CCs, when in HBs and during navigating between HBs the RTV emissions may become to be a dominating. In HBs it was found also a contribution from the radiophones and local WiFi hot spots which may need attention. Observed differences in frequency pattern of EMR exposures in CCs and HBs is significant in the view of required measurement devices and protocols for studies on the EMR exposure in HBs.

articleTitle: High frequency measurement and simulation of electromagnetic interference filters
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The aim of this paper is to improve the circuit modeling of electromagnetic interference (EMI) filters by taking into account near-field inductive couplings using additional 3D modeling. In this work a method is described with which the equivalent circuit model of an EMI filter—given its components have already been selected—can be specified using measurement setups, where only an impedance analyzer is required.It is also demonstrated, how the couplings between the components (mainly mutual inductances) are extracted from 3D electromagnetic simulations. Furthermore, the additional couplings caused by the leads and wires are also considered in the model. This technique can be utilized to tune the circuit model of the filter for the changing topology, which is a common problem, for instance in the automotive industry.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study of a Graphene-Loaded Composite for Improved EMI Performance of Satellite Cavities
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The continuous development of lightweight composites with enhanced electromagnetic properties remains a persisting challenge in satellite applications. To address this issue, the integration of a graphene-filled polymeric paint has been proposed as a feasible solution for controlling electromagnetic interference (EMI) effects, particularly in satellite scenarios where the smaller size and reduced cost compared to standard electromagnetic shields can offer significant advantages. In this paper, the electric field generated by the spurious emissions from internal units of a Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite operating at 162 MHz is evaluated, and the successful integration of a graphene-filled polymeric paint within a satellite cavity to mitigate EMI on the Automatic Identification System (AIS) receiver unit is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Efficient In situ Assessment of Radiated Emissions using Time-Domain Measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents three different case studies where the electromagnetic emissions of atypical equipment (a photovoltaic system, a passenger boarding bridge and a pallet washing machine) have been assessed in situ using time-domain measurement systems. The magnetic field (150 kHz-30 MHz) and electric field (30 MHz-1 GHz) emissions are considered. The technical challenges encountered and the solutions adopted for each scenario will be highlighted by describing the methodology employed. The goal is to relate the empirical knowledge and know-how gained through those study cases with the specific requirements and procedures defined in the standards. In that sense, multi-channel time-domain emissions measurements have been essential to carry out those measurement campaigns efficiently. The results are summarised as lessons learned during the experiences reported in this article. This work is relevant to support the revision or development of standards about in situ EMC testing as it provides helpful evidence to validate alternative radiated emissions measurement methods under realistic conditions.

articleTitle: Common-mode Current Converted from PLC Signal in Three-phase Distribution Network with Earth Leakage Circuit Breaker
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: It is known that power line communication (PLC) works across different phases in a three-wire three-phase distribution system; even through the pairs of lines for each phase are not physically connected. This research focuses on the distribution boards in the power distribution network and evaluates the effect on PLC of an earth leakage circuit breaker(ELCB) attached to the boards. The results of an evaluation of the common-mode current with and without the ELCB showed that it increased with the ELCB. Resonance in our setup occured at 20 MHz. A simulation analysis showed that the capacitor connecting the two wires at both ends of the ELCB contributed to the resonance.

articleTitle: PEEC Solution of EM-Circuit Problems for Combined Metalic and Dielectric Structures Based on the Augmented Integral Equations
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents a full-wave triangular mesh based partial element equivalent circuit (PEEC) approach in the frequency domain for combined metal-dielectric structures based on A-PMCHWT and E-PMCHWT formulations of the augmented electric field integral equation (A-EFIE). The method avoids so called low frequency breakdown of EFIE and takes into account phase shifts of fields radiated by partial elements. 3D structures are described with equivalent circuit that can be combined with circuit or S-parameter models of electronic components. Validation of the proposed solution is done for toroidal choke in common and differential modes via comparison of obtained results with measurements and with standard MoM in the frequency range from 1Hz to 100MHz.

articleTitle: Circuit Prediction Model of Electric Field Emission of a Vehicle-mounted Three-phase DC/AC Inverter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The high-voltage inverter-motor drive system in an electric vehicle is easily to produce strong electric field radiation, which endangers the stable operation of surrounding sensitive electronic equipment. This paper analyzes the common-mode (CM) current paths and its spatial electric field of a vehicle-mounted three-phase inverter-motor system, and proposes a lumped circuit model including CM voltage sources, power cables and pole antenna receiver. The circuit model predicts the electric field emission in the 150 kHz-30 MHz frequency band and is verified by experiment results. In the end, the shielded power cable design is proposed to suppress the electric field radiation.

articleTitle: SNR Improvement for Heart Rate Estimation Using mmWave 79 GHz FMCW MIMO Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Recently, interest in various engineering technologies for medical purposes has been increasing. Various biometric information can be obtained by remotely sensing signals of a human body using a radar. Typically, remote recording of heart movements allows researchers to calculate the heart rate and infer the heart condition. In addition, through these algorithms, it is possible to provide doctors with a non-face-to-face treatment support system for real-time monitoring information such as patients with heart disease. In this article, we will outline a novel mathematical model for extracting the cardiac signal utilizing the analytic signal argument of the inphase channel. The power spectral density of the latter will then be used to measure the heart rate. Raw data are extracted from a Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) 79 GHz Frequency-Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar designed in our laboratory. In order to evaluate the performance of our model, we also collected heart rate reference values using a wearable device called a photoplethysmograph (PPG). Finally, we made a comparison between our proposed method and the conventional method based on signal spectrum analysis. The outcomes demonstrate that, for our use case, our suggested procedure worked better than the conventional approach and significantly increased the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).

articleTitle: Definition And Characterization Of An Electromagnetic Operational Domain Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The increasing use of autonomy and complexity of systems has identified the need for explicit specification of operational conditions for systems such that the properties of a system can be assured against these conditions. Although the EE (Electromagnetic Environment) within which a system can safely operate should be considered as part of operational conditions, it has not previously been represented in taxonomies of ODMs (Operational Domain Models). In this paper, the concept of EODM (Electromagnetic Operational Domain Model) is introduced which facilitates the development and safe operation of a system against the safety risks emerging from EMI (Electromagnetic Interference). Furthermore, a process for defining the EODM during development of a system is presented, and an appropriate process for considering EODM’s contribution during operation is proposed.

articleTitle: Measurement of Radiation Patterns for Ultra-Broadband Folded Long-Hexagon Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: In EMI measurements, measuring antennas are needed to be changed according to the frequency bands. Antenna replacement is a factor that increases the time and effort required for measuring and leads to higher measurement costs. Therefore, aiming to perform EMI measurements over the entire frequency band with a single antenna, a folded long-hexagon antenna (FLHA) had been designed and developed in the previous study. The characteristics of the developed antenna, including absolute antenna gain, were measured in the previous study and the usable frequency of the antenna was shown to be from 400 MHz to 40 GHz. However, to determine whether this antenna can be used for EMI measurements, the radiation patterns have also to be evaluated over the entire frequency band. This paper presents a measurement result of the radiation patterns of the developed antenna and discusses its suitability for EMI measurements.

articleTitle: Unexpected Common Mode Choke Saturation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of common mode choke (CMC) saturation. Next to a phenomenon of CMC saturation due to leakage inductance, a saturation caused by unbalanced impedance leading to mode conversion is discussed. A measurement setup mimicking the unbalanced condition, evaluating the saturation of the CMC under the dc bias is presented. Several CMCs made with nanocrystalline and ferrite cores, of various core sizes and a number of turns have been evaluated.

articleTitle: Investigation of Real Dynamic Automotive Electromagnetic Environment Measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Due to the continuous expansion of technologies onto modern vehicles such as e.g., autonomous driving, wireless communications, electric powertrain etc. the on-board electronic equipment increase rapidly. This results in complex electromagnetic environments at the interior of car cabins. This non-stop implementation of electronic equipment requires further investigation of real dynamic automotive environments so that potential electromagnetic threats caused by internal and/or external sources can be identified and overcome. In this paper, the electromagnetic environment of a combustion engine car is investigated and evaluated. The received values taken inside a combustion engine car are examined following two different techniques: the fixed-position technique and the random-walk technique. The measurements are performed in two different states of the car: parked and on the move. The raw results of all the cases are extensively discussed to address how these techniques can provide information of various real conditions. Later, this information can be used for assuring electromagnetic compatibility and risk mitigation.

articleTitle: Control equipment in the unique EMC environment of High Current Testing Laboratory, case study
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: The High Current Testing Laboratory (HCTL) must be safe for the operational staff. Moreover, equipment supervising the test must operate without any malfunctions. It was observed that the time-phase controller used for supervising the test gets sporadically out of control, in the HCTL under consideration. Investigation of the EMC environment showed its uniqueness in the considered HCTL. Therefore individual, specific EMC test program was elaborated. The time-phase controller did not pass this program. Consequently, the need for a new, robust time-phase controller arose. In turn this resulted in a development, construction and assembling of the new device. The new one passed the previously prepared test program. Although an individual case is presented in the paper, general hints useful both in development of the control equipment and planning as well as organisation of the HCTL are formulated in the conclusions.

articleTitle: Measurement of Impulsive Electromagnetic Field Caused by ESD Using A Folded Long-Hexagon Antenna and It’s Transient Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility – EMC Europe
abstract: Impulsive transient electromagnetic fields caused by electrostatic discharge (ESD) have a serious influence on modern IT high-tech equipment.
